title.zh: 卷八十一 列傳第四十一 劉秀之 顧琛 顧覬之
title.en: Volume 81 Biographies 41: Liu Xiuzhi, Gu Chen, Gu Jizhi
title.raw: 卷八十一 列傳第四十一 劉秀之 顧琛 顧覬之 Volume 81 Biographies 41: Liu Xiuzhi, Gu Chen, Gu Jizhi

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十一 劉秀之 顧琛 顧覬之

translations.literal: Biographies 41: Liu Xiuzhi, Gu Chen, Gu Jizhi
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 41: Liu Xiuzhi, Gu Chen, and Gu Jizhi

sentences.zh: 劉秀之，字道寶，東莞莒人，司徒劉穆之從兄子也，世居京口。

translations.literal: Liu Xiuzhi, style name Daobao, was a man of Juxian in Dongguan commandery, a nephew of the Chief Minister Liu Muzhi on the fraternal line; his family had long dwelt at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiuzhi, whose style was Daobao, came from Juxian in Dongguan. He was a nephew of Chief Minister Liu Muzhi by the fraternal line, and his family had lived at Jingkou for generations.

sentences.zh: 祖爽，尚書都官郎，山陰令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shuang was a Director in the Capital Crimes section of the Secretariat and magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shuang had served as a director in the Secretariat's capital-crimes office and as magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 父仲道，高祖克京城，以補建武參軍，與孟昶留守，事定，以為余姚令，卒官。

translations.literal: His father Zhongdao, when Emperor Gaozu captured the capital region, was appointed as an aide in the Jianwu command; together with Meng Chang he remained to guard the city; when affairs were settled he was made magistrate of Yuyao and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongdao, when Emperor Gaozu took the capital, was appointed an aide in the Jianwu command and stayed behind with Meng Chang to hold the city. After order was restored he became magistrate of Yuyao and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 秀子少孤貧，有志操。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi in youth was orphaned and poor, yet possessed resolve and moral fiber.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi lost his father early and grew up poor, but he possessed firm resolve and moral character.

sentences.zh: 十許歲時，與諸兒戲於前渚，忽有大蛇來，勢甚猛，莫不顛沛驚呼，秀之獨不動，眾並異焉。

translations.literal: When he was about ten, playing with other boys on the foreshore, suddenly a great serpent came—its force very fierce—and none failed to panic and cry out; Xiuzhi alone did not move, and all found it strange.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about ten, he was playing with other boys on the riverbank when a huge serpent suddenly appeared, fierce and terrifying. The others all fled in panic, but Xiuzhi alone stood still, and everyone marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 東海何承天雅相知器，以女妻之。

translations.literal: He Chengtian of Donghai held him in esteem and knew his capacity, and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian of Donghai recognized his talent and held him in high regard, and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 兄欽之為硃齡石右軍參軍，隨齡石敗沒，秀之哀戚，不歡宴者十年。

translations.literal: His elder brother Qin was staff officer to Zhu Lingce's Right Army; following Lingce to defeat he perished; Xiuzhi mourned deeply and for ten years did not partake in feasts.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Qin had been a staff officer in Zhu Lingce's Right Army and died when Lingce's forces were destroyed. Xiuzhi grieved deeply and for ten years refused all banquets and revelry.

sentences.zh: 景平二年，除駙馬都尉、奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingping he was appointed Commander of the Stable for Imperial Sons-in-law and Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jingping era he was appointed Commander of the Stable for Imperial Sons-in-law and made an Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 家貧，求為廣陵郡丞。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he requested to serve as assistant magistrate of Guangling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Because his family was poor, he asked to be made assistant magistrate of Guangling commandery.

sentences.zh: 仍除撫軍江夏王義恭、平北彭城王義康行參軍，出為無錫、陽羨、烏程令，並著能名。

translations.literal: He was then appointed acting staff officer to the General Who Pacifies the Army, Prince of Jiangxia, and to the Northern Pacification Prince of Pengcheng; he went out as magistrate of Wuxi, Yangxian, and Wucheng in succession, and at each post won renown for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made acting staff officer to Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, General Who Pacifies the Army, and to Prince Yikang of Pengcheng, General Who Pacifies the North. He then served in succession as magistrate of Wuxi, Yangxian, and Wucheng, winning a reputation for ability at each post.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十六年，遷建康令，除尚書中兵郎，重除建康。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to magistrate of Jiankang, appointed Middle Officer for Troops in the Secretariat, and again appointed magistrate of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to magistrate of Jiankang, appointed Middle Officer for Troops in the Secretariat, and then appointed magistrate of Jiankang a second time.

sentences.zh: 性纖密，善糾摘微隱，政甚有聲。

translations.literal: By nature meticulous, skilled at uncovering minute wrongs, his administration won great repute.
translations.idiomatic: Meticulous by nature and skilled at exposing even the smallest irregularities, he governed with a reputation that rang far and wide.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書沈演之每稱之于太祖。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Civil Service, Shen Yanzhi, repeatedly praised him to Emperor Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yanzhi, Minister of the Civil Service, spoke of him repeatedly to Emperor Taizu with high praise.

sentences.zh: 世祖鎮襄陽，以為撫軍錄事參軍、襄陽令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu held Xiangyang, he made him Recording Officer on the Pacifying Army staff and magistrate of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu was stationed at Xiangyang, he appointed Xiuzhi Recording Officer on the Pacifying Army staff and magistrate of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 襄陽有六門堰，良田數千頃，堰久決壞，公私廢業。

translations.literal: Xiangyang had the Six-Gates Weir, with several thousand qing of fine fields; the weir had long broken and collapsed, and public and private uses lay idle.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang had the Six-Gates Weir, which irrigated several thousand qing of fertile land, but the weir had long since burst and collapsed, leaving both public and private fields abandoned.

sentences.zh: 世祖遣秀之修復，雍部由是大豐。

translations.literal: Shizu sent Xiuzhi to restore it, and Yong Province thereby became greatly prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu sent Xiuzhi to repair the weir, and Yong Province thereafter enjoyed a great harvest.

sentences.zh: 改領廣平太守。

translations.literal: He was changed to concurrent commandery governor of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to serve concurrently as governor of Guangping commandery.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，除督梁、南北秦三州諸軍事、甯遠將軍、西戎校尉、梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: In year twenty-five he was appointed Supervisor of military affairs for Liang and North and South Qin, General Pacifying the Distance, Commandant of the Western Rong, and provincial governor of Liang and South Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed to supervise military affairs in Liang and the three Qin provinces, with the rank of General Pacifying the Distance, as Commandant of the Western Rong, and as provincial governor of Liang and South Qin.

sentences.zh: 時漢川饑儉，境內騷然，秀之善於為政，躬自儉約。

translations.literal: At the time the Han River region suffered famine; the territory was unsettled; Xiuzhi was skilled in governance and personally practiced austerity.
translations.idiomatic: Famine had struck the Han River region and the territory was in turmoil. Xiuzhi governed with skill and practiced austerity himself.

sentences.zh: 先是，漢川悉以絹為貨，秀之限令用錢，百姓至今受其利。

translations.literal: Previously the Han River region used silk entirely as currency; Xiuzhi restricted orders to use coin, and the people to this day benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Han River region had used silk as its sole medium of exchange. Xiuzhi restricted trade to coin, and the people still benefit from that reform today.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，大舉北伐，遣輔國將軍楊文德、巴西、梓潼二郡太守劉弘宗受秀之節度，震盪汧、隴。

translations.literal: In year twenty-seven a great northern campaign was launched; the Assisting State General Yang Wende and the governors of Ba and Zitong, Liu Hongzong, were placed under Xiuzhi's command and shook Qian and Long.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year the court launched a major northern campaign. The Assisting State General Yang Wende and Liu Hongzong, governor of the Ba and Zitong commanderies, were placed under Xiuzhi's command and drove deep into the Qian and Long regions.

sentences.zh: 秀之遣建武將軍錫千秋二千人向子午谷南口，府司馬竺宗之三千人向駱谷南口，威遠將軍梁尋千人向斜谷南口。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi sent the Establishing Martial General Xi Qianqiu with two thousand men toward the southern mouth of Ziwu Valley, the prefectural marshal Zhu Zongzhi with three thousand toward the southern mouth of Luo Valley, and the Prestigious Distance General Liang Xun with one thousand toward the southern mouth of Xie Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi sent the Establishing Martial General Xi Qianqiu with two thousand men toward the southern mouth of Ziwu Valley, the prefectural marshal Zhu Zongzhi with three thousand toward the southern mouth of Luo Valley, and the Prestigious Distance General Liang Xun with one thousand toward the southern mouth of Xie Valley.

sentences.zh: 氐賊楊高為寇，秀之討之，斬高兄弟。

translations.literal: The Di bandit Yang Gao raided as a marauder; Xiuzhi campaigned against him and beheaded Gao and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The Di chieftain Yang Gao had been raiding the borders. Xiuzhi campaigned against him and beheaded Gao and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 元兇弑逆，秀之聞問，即日起兵，求率眾赴襄陽，司空南譙王義宣不許。

translations.literal: When the usurper committed regicide, Xiuzhi upon hearing the news immediately raised troops and asked to lead his forces to Xiangyang; the Minister of Works, Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan, did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When the usurper murdered the emperor, Xiuzhi heard the news and immediately mobilized his troops, asking permission to march to Xiangyang. Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao, Minister of Works, refused.

sentences.zh: 事寧，遷使持節、督益甯二州諸軍事、甯朔將軍、益州刺史。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of military affairs in Yi and Ning, General Pacifying the North, and governor of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored he was promoted to Bearer of the Staff, placed in charge of military affairs in Yi and Ning, given the rank of General Pacifying the North, and appointed governor of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 折留俸祿二百八十萬，付梁州鎮庫，此外蕭然。

translations.literal: He set aside salary of 2.8 million and delivered it to the Liangzhou garrison treasury; beyond that he had nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He set aside 2.8 million in salary and deposited it in the Liangzhou garrison treasury; apart from that he left with nothing.

sentences.zh: 梁、益二州土境豐富，前後刺史，莫不營聚蓄，多者致萬金。

translations.literal: Liang and Yi were rich in territory; successive governors none failed to amass stores, some accumulating ten thousand in gold.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Yi were wealthy provinces, and successive governors had all hoarded riches—some amassing as much as ten thousand in gold.

sentences.zh: 所攜賓僚，並京邑貧士，出為郡縣，皆以苟得自資。

translations.literal: The retainers and staff he brought were all poor scholars from the capital; when they went out to commanderies and counties, all used unscrupulous gain to enrich themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The aides and staff members governors typically brought from the capital were poor scholars who, once posted to the counties, enriched themselves by any means they could.

sentences.zh: 秀之為治整肅，以身率下，遠近安悅焉。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi governed with stern order, leading subordinates by his own example, and near and far were content and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi governed with strict discipline and led by example. People near and far were content under his rule.

sentences.zh: 南譙王義宣據荊州為逆，遣參軍王曜徵兵於秀之，秀之即日斬曜戒嚴。

translations.literal: Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan held Jingzhou in rebellion and sent his staff officer Wang Yao to levy troops from Xiuzhi; Xiuzhi that same day beheaded Yao and declared martial alert.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao seized Jingzhou in rebellion and sent his staff officer Wang Yao to demand troops from Xiuzhi. Xiuzhi beheaded Yao that same day and put his forces on full alert.

sentences.zh: 遣中兵參軍韋山松萬人襲江陵，出峽。

translations.literal: He sent the Middle Troops Officer Wei Shansong with ten thousand men to strike Jiangling, exiting through the gorges.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the Middle Troops Officer Wei Shansong with ten thousand men to strike at Jiangling through the gorges.

sentences.zh: 竺超民遣將席天生逆之，山松一戰，即梟其首。

translations.literal: Zhu Chaomin sent the general Xi Tiansheng to oppose him; in one battle Shansong took his head.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Chaomin sent the general Xi Tiansheng to block him. Shansong defeated him in a single engagement and took his head.

sentences.zh: 進至江陵，為魯爽所敗，山松見殺。

translations.literal: Advancing to Jiangling, he was defeated by Lu Shuang; Shansong was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When he advanced to Jiangling he was defeated by Lu Shuang, and Shansong was killed.

sentences.zh: 其年，進號征虜將軍，改督為監，持節、刺史如故，以起義功，封康樂縣侯，食邑六百戶。

translations.literal: That year his title was advanced to General Who Captures Barbarians; Supervisor was changed to Overseer; Bearer of the Staff and provincial governor as before; for merit in the righteous rising he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Kangle county with a fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was promoted to General Who Captures Barbarians, his title of Supervisor changed to Overseer, while he retained the Staff and his governorship. For his service in the righteous rising he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Kangle with a fief of six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷監郢州諸軍事、郢州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Overseer of military affairs in Yingzhou and governor of Yingzhou; his general's rank was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to oversee military affairs in Yingzhou and appointed governor of Yingzhou, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 未就。

translations.literal: He did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He never took up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 五年，雍州刺史海陵王休茂反，為土人所誅，遣秀之以本官慰勞，分別善惡。

translations.literal: In year five the governor of Yongzhou, Prince of Hailing Xiumao, rebelled and was killed by local people; Xiuzhi was sent in his original office to comfort and reassure, distinguishing good from evil.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Prince Xiumao of Hailing, governor of Yongzhou, rebelled and was killed by the local populace. The court sent Xiuzhi in his existing capacity to comfort the region and distinguish the innocent from the guilty.

sentences.zh: 事畢還都，出為使持節、散騎常侍、都督雍、梁、南北秦四州、郢州之竟陵、隨二郡諸軍事、安北將軍、甯蠻校尉、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: When the mission was done he returned to the capital, then went out as Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander of military affairs in Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, and the Jingling and Sui commanderies of Yingzhou, General Who Pacifies the North, Commandant Pacifying the Man, and governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his mission was complete he returned to the capital, then was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander of military affairs in Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, and the Jingling and Sui districts of Yingzhou, with the rank of General Who Pacifies the North, as Commandant Pacifying the Man, and as governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 上車駕幸新亭，視秀之發引，將征為左僕射，事未行，八年卒，時年六十八。

translations.literal: The emperor's carriage went to Xinting to see Xiuzhi's departure; he was about to be summoned as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, but before the matter could proceed he died in year eight at age sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went in person to Xinting to see Xiuzhi off on his departure. He was about to be summoned as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, but before the appointment could take effect Xiuzhi died in the eighth year, at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 上甚痛惜之，詔曰：「秀之識局明遠，才應通暢，誠著蕃朝，績宣累嶽。

translations.literal: The emperor grieved deeply and issued an edict: "Xiuzhi's vision and grasp were clear and far-reaching, his talent responsive and fluent; his loyalty was manifest at court, his achievements proclaimed across many ranges.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved deeply and issued an edict: "Xiuzhi's vision was clear and far-reaching, his talent responsive and fluent. His loyalty was manifest at court, and his achievements resounded across the frontier ranges.

sentences.zh: 往歲逆臣交構，首義萬里，及職司端尹，贊戎兩宮，嘉謀征譽，實彰朝野。

translations.literal: In years past when rebellious ministers conspired, he took the lead in righteous action ten thousand li away; when he held the key office at the center, he aided the Two Palaces in military affairs—his fine counsel and gathered renown were truly manifest at court and in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellious ministers conspired in years past, he took the lead in righteous action a thousand miles from the capital. When he held a key post at court he aided the Two Palaces in military affairs. His counsel and his renown were manifest to all, within the palace and beyond.

sentences.zh: 漢南法繁民嗛，屬佇良牧，故暫輟心膂，外弘風規，出未逾期，德庇西服。

translations.literal: South of the Han the laws were many and the people frugal; they depended on a good shepherd, so for a time we paused our heart and backbone, sending him abroad to spread standards of conduct—he had not been out a full term before his virtue sheltered the western dress.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Han the laws were burdensome and the people frugal; they needed a capable governor. We therefore set aside our most trusted minister to carry our standards to the frontier. He had not been gone a full term before his virtue sheltered the western provinces.

sentences.zh: 詳考古烈，旅觀終始，淳心忠概，無以尚茲。

translations.literal: Examining ancient worthies in detail and surveying beginnings and ends together, his pure heart and loyal resolve—none can surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying the great men of old and weighing their lives from beginning to end, his pure heart and loyal resolve surpass them all.

sentences.zh: 方式亮皇猷，入衛根本，奄至薨逝，震慟於朕心。

translations.literal: His manner would have illuminated the imperial design and entered to guard the root; suddenly he passed away, shaking and grieving my heart.
translations.idiomatic: His manner would have illuminated the imperial design and guarded the foundations of the state. His sudden death shakes and grieves my heart.

sentences.zh: 生榮之典，未窮寵數，哀終之禮，宜盡崇飾。

translations.literal: The honors of life had not exhausted the measure of favor; the rites of mourning should be fully elevated and adorned.
translations.idiomatic: The honors of his life had not exhausted the measure of our favor; the rites of mourning should be elevated to the fullest degree.

sentences.zh: 兼履謙守約，封社弗廣，興言悼往，益增痛恨。

translations.literal: Moreover he practiced humility and kept to austerity; his enfeoffment was not broad—speaking of this in mourning the past, my regret only increases.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he practiced humility and lived in austerity; his enfeoffment was never broad. Speaking of him in grief, my regret only deepens.

sentences.zh: 可贈侍中、司空，持節、都督、刺史、校尉如故，並增封邑為千戶。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Works; Bearer of the Staff, Commander, governor, and Commandant as before; and his fief increased to one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously granted Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Works, retaining the Staff, his command, his governorship, and his commandancy, and let his fief be increased to one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 諡為忠成公。」

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Loyal and Accomplished Duke."
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title shall be Loyal and Accomplished Duke."

sentences.zh: 秀之野率無風采，而心力堅正。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi was rustic and unadorned in bearing, yet his mind and strength were firm and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi was plain and unassuming in manner, but his resolve was firm and his integrity unwavering.

sentences.zh: 上以其蒞官清潔，家無餘財，賜錢二十萬，布三百匹。

translations.literal: Because he had served in office with purity and his household had no surplus wealth, the emperor granted two hundred thousand in cash and three hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had served with integrity and left his household without surplus wealth, the emperor granted two hundred thousand in cash and three hundred bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 子景遠嗣，官至前軍將軍。

translations.literal: His son Jingyuan succeeded him and reached the post of General of the Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingyuan succeeded to the title and rose to the rank of General of the Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 景遠卒，子俊，齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: Jingyuan died; his son Jun—when Qi received the abdication, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingyuan died, his son Jun held the title until Qi received the abdication, at which point the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 秀之弟粹之，晉陵太守。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi's younger brother Cuizhi was governor of Jinling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi's younger brother Cuizhi served as governor of Jinling commandery.

sentences.zh: 顧琛，字弘瑋，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Gu Chen, style name Hongwei, was a man of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Chen, whose style was Hongwei, came from Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖和，晉司空。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather He was Jin Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather He had served as Minister of Works under Jin.

sentences.zh: 祖履之，父惔，並為司徒左西掾。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lüzhi and father Tan both served as Left Western Aide to the Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lüzhi and his father Tan had both served as Left Western Aide to the Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 琛謹確不尚浮華，起家州從事，駙馬都尉，奉朝請。

translations.literal: Chen was cautious and solid, not given to display; he began his career as provincial aide, Commander of the Stable for Imperial Sons-in-law, and Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was cautious and solid by nature, with no taste for ostentation. He began his career as a provincial aide, then served as Commander of the Stable for Imperial Sons-in-law and as Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 少帝景平中，太皇太后崩，除大匠丞。

translations.literal: During the Jingping era of Emperor Shao, when the Grand Empress Dowager died, he was appointed Assistant Director of the Imperial Works.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingping era of Emperor Shao, when the Grand Empress Dowager died, he was appointed Assistant Director of the Imperial Works.

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康右軍驃騎參軍，晉陵令，司徒參軍，尚書庫部郎，本邑中正。

translations.literal: Staff officer to Prince of Pengcheng Yikang's Right Army and Rapid Cavalry, magistrate of Jinling, staff officer to the Chief Minister, Secretariat Officer in the Arsenal section, and local Rectifier for his native district.
translations.idiomatic: He served as staff officer in Prince Yikang of Pengcheng's Right Army and Rapid Cavalry, as magistrate of Jinling, as staff officer to the Chief Minister, as an officer in the Secretariat's arsenal section, and as Rectifier for his native district.

sentences.zh: 元嘉七年，太祖遣到彥之經略河南，大敗，悉委棄兵甲，武庫為之空虛。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanjia Emperor Taizu sent Dao Yanzhi to take control of the region south of the Yellow River; he suffered a great defeat and abandoned all arms and armor, and the arsenal was left empty.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yuanjia Emperor Taizu sent Dao Yanzhi to secure the region south of the Yellow River. The campaign ended in disaster, with all arms and armor abandoned, and the arsenal left empty.

sentences.zh: 後太祖宴會，有荒外歸化人在坐，上問琛：「庫中仗猶有幾許？」

translations.literal: Later at a banquet of Taizu, a man from beyond the wilds who had submitted to civilization was seated; the emperor asked Chen: "How many weapons remain in the arsenal?"
translations.idiomatic: Later, at one of Taizu's banquets, a tribesman from beyond the frontier who had submitted to the dynasty was present. The emperor turned to Chen and asked, "How many weapons remain in the arsenal?"

sentences.zh: 琛詭答：「有十萬人仗。」

translations.literal: Chen answered deceptively: "There are arms for one hundred thousand men."
translations.idiomatic: Chen answered evasively, "Enough arms for one hundred thousand men."

sentences.zh: 舊武庫仗秘不言多少，上既發問，追悔失言，及琛詭對，上甚喜。

translations.literal: By old custom the arsenal's arms were secret and their number not spoken; the emperor having raised the question regretted his slip of speech, but when Chen answered deceptively the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the arsenal's stores were kept secret and their numbers never disclosed. The emperor, having spoken, immediately regretted his indiscretion—but when Chen gave his evasive answer, the emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 尚書寺門有制，八座以下門生隨入者各有差，不得雜以人士。

translations.literal: The Secretariat gate had regulations: retainers who entered with officials below the Eight Seats each had their distinctions and might not be mixed with outside persons.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations at the Secretariat gate stipulated that retainers accompanying officials below the Eight Seats were admitted according to rank and might not be mingled with outsiders.

sentences.zh: 琛以宗人顧碩頭寄尚書張茂度門名，而與碩頭同席坐。

translations.literal: Chen had his clansman Gu Shuotou registered under the gate-name of Secretariat officer Zhang Maodu, yet sat at the same mat with Shuotou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen had registered his clansman Gu Shuotou under the gate-name of Secretariat officer Zhang Maodu, yet sat at the same mat with Shuotou.

sentences.zh: 明年，坐遣出，免中正。

translations.literal: The next year, on this charge he was expelled and dismissed as Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was expelled on this charge and stripped of his post as Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 凡尚書官，大罪則免，小罪則遣出。

translations.literal: As a rule for Secretariat officers, great offenses meant dismissal, small offenses meant expulsion.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, great offenses among Secretariat officers resulted in dismissal, while lesser offenses resulted in temporary expulsion.

sentences.zh: 遣出者，百日無代人，聽還本職。

translations.literal: Those expelled, if for one hundred days no one replaced them, were permitted to return to their original posts.
translations.idiomatic: An expelled officer who went unreplaced for one hundred days was permitted to return to his original post.

sentences.zh: 琛仍為彭城王義康所請，補司徒錄事參軍，山陰令，複為司徒錄事，遷少府。

translations.literal: Chen was again invited by Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, appointed Recording Officer on the Chief Minister's staff, magistrate of Shanyin, again Recording Officer, and transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Privy Purse.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was again invited by Prince Yikang of Pengcheng and appointed Recording Officer on the Chief Minister's staff and magistrate of Shanyin. He served again as Recording Officer and was then transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Privy Purse.

sentences.zh: 十五年，出為義興太守。

translations.literal: In year fifteen he went out as governor of Yixing commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was sent out as governor of Yixing commandery.

sentences.zh: 初，義康請琛入府，欲委以腹心，琛不能承事劉湛，故尋見斥外。

translations.literal: At first Yikang invited Chen into his household, wishing to entrust him as a trusted confidant; Chen could not serve under Liu Zhan, and so before long was cast out.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yikang had invited Chen into his household, intending to make him a trusted confidant. Chen could not work under Liu Zhan, however, and was soon cast aside.

sentences.zh: 十九年，徙東陽太守，欲使琛防守大將軍彭城王義康，固辭忤旨，廢黜還家積年。

translations.literal: In year nineteen he was transferred to governor of Dongyang, intending that Chen guard against the Grand General, Prince of Pengcheng Yikang; he firmly declined, offending the imperial will, and was dismissed and returned home for many years.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was transferred to governor of Dongyang, the court intending that he keep watch over Grand General Prince Yikang of Pengcheng. Chen firmly declined, offending the emperor, and was dismissed. He remained at home for many years.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，索虜南至瓜步，權假琛建威將軍。

translations.literal: In year twenty-seven the northern enemy reached south to Guabu; Chen was provisionally granted the title General Establishing Prestige.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year the northern enemy advanced as far south as Guabu, and Chen was provisionally granted the rank of General Establishing Prestige.

sentences.zh: 尋除東海王禕冠軍司馬，行會稽郡事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Champion Staff Officer to Prince of Donghai Yi and acted in the affairs of Kuaiji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Champion Staff Officer to Prince Yi of Donghai and placed in charge of Kuaiji commandery affairs.

sentences.zh: 隨王誕代禕，複為誕安東司馬。

translations.literal: Prince of Sui Dan replaced Yi; Chen again served as Dan's Pacifying the East Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Dan of Sui replaced Yi, Chen again served as Dan's Pacifying the East Staff Officer.

sentences.zh: 元兇弑立，分會稽五郡置會州，以誕為刺史，即以琛為會稽太守，加五品將軍，置將佐。

translations.literal: When the usurper murdered and enthroned himself, the five commanderies of Kuaiji were split to establish Kuai Province; Dan was made governor, and Chen was immediately made governor of Kuaiji, with addition of fifth-rank general and appointment of generals and aides.
translations.idiomatic: When the usurper murdered the emperor and seized the throne, the five Kuaiji commanderies were reorganized into Kuai Province with Dan as governor. Chen was immediately appointed governor of Kuaiji, given fifth-rank general's rank, and provided with generals and staff.

sentences.zh: 誕起義，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Dan raised the righteous standard, Chen was advanced to Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan joined the righteous rising, Chen was promoted to Champion General.

sentences.zh: 事平，遷吳興太守。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was transferred to governor of Wuxing commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored he was transferred to governor of Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年，征為五兵尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaojian he was summoned as Minister of the Five Troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiaojian he was summoned to the capital as Minister of the Five Troops.

sentences.zh: 未拜，複為甯朔將軍、吳郡太守。

translations.literal: Before he could accept the appointment he was again made General Pacifying the North and governor of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up that post he was again appointed General Pacifying the North and governor of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 以起義功，封永新縣五等侯。

translations.literal: For merit in the righteous rising he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Yongxin county.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in the righteous rising he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Yongxin.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，吳縣令張闓坐居母喪無禮，下廷尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming the magistrate of Wu county, Zhang Kai, was charged with lacking propriety while in mourning for his mother and sent to the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daming the magistrate of Wu county, Zhang Kai, was charged with impropriety during mourning for his mother and referred to the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 錢唐令沈文秀判劾違謬，應坐被彈。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Qiantang, Shen Wenxiu, in judging and impeaching had erred; he should have been charged and impeached himself.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Qiantang, Shen Wenxiu, had erred in his judgment and impeachment and should himself have been charged.

sentences.zh: 琛宣言於眾：「闓被劾之始，屢相申明。」

translations.literal: Chen declared before the assembly: "From the beginning of Kai's impeachment I repeatedly explained on his behalf."
translations.idiomatic: Chen declared publicly, "From the moment Kai was impeached I repeatedly spoke in his defense."

sentences.zh: 又云：「當啟文秀留縣。」

translations.literal: He also said: "I shall memorialize to have Wenxiu kept at his county."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "I intend to memorialize to have Wenxiu kept at his post in the county."

sentences.zh: 世祖聞之大怒，謂琛賣惡歸上，免官。

translations.literal: When Shizu heard this he was greatly enraged, saying Chen was shifting blame onto the throne, and dismissed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu heard this he was furious, accusing Chen of shifting blame onto the throne, and dismissed him from office.

sentences.zh: 琛母老，仍停家。

translations.literal: Chen's mother was old; he remained at home.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's mother was elderly, so he remained at home to care for her.

sentences.zh: 琛及前西陽太守張牧，並司空竟陵王誕故佐，誕待琛等素厚。

translations.literal: Chen and the former governor of Xiyang, Zhang Mu, were both former aides of the Minister of Works, Prince of Jingling Dan; Dan had always treated Chen and the others with great kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Chen and the former governor of Xiyang, Zhang Mu, had both served as aides to Prince Dan of Jingling when he was Minister of Works. Dan had always treated Chen and the others with great kindness.

sentences.zh: 三年，誕據廣陵反，遣客陸延稔齎書板琛為征南將軍，牧為安東將軍，琛子前尚書郎寶素為諮議參軍，寶素弟前司空參軍寶先為從事中郎，牧兄前吳郡丞濟為冠軍將軍，從弟前司空主簿晏為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: In year three Dan held Guangling in rebellion and sent his agent Lu Yannian bearing appointment tablets making Chen General Campaigning South, Mu General Pacifying the East, Chen's son the former Secretariat Gentleman Baosu as Advising Officer, Baosu's younger brother the former Chief Minister's staff officer Baoxian as Attendant Gentleman, Mu's elder brother the former Wu commandery aide Ji as Champion General, and Mu's younger cousin the former Chief Minister's registrar Yan as Advising Officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Dan seized Guangling in rebellion and sent his agent Lu Yannian with appointment tablets offering Chen the rank of General Campaigning South, Mu the rank of General Pacifying the East, Chen's son Baosu (formerly a Secretariat Gentleman) the post of Advising Officer, Baosu's younger brother Baoxian (formerly on the Chief Minister's staff) Attendant Gentleman, Mu's elder brother Ji (formerly aide in Wu commandery) Champion General, and Mu's younger cousin Yan (formerly registrar to the Chief Minister) Advising Officer.

sentences.zh: 時世祖以琛素結事誕，或有異志，遣使就吳郡太守王曇生誅琛父子。

translations.literal: At the time Shizu, because Chen had long been bound in service to Dan, suspected he might harbor a different intent, and sent an envoy to the governor of Wu commandery, Wang Tansheng, to execute Chen and his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu, knowing Chen's long association with Dan, suspected disloyalty and sent an envoy to Wang Tansheng, governor of Wu commandery, ordering the execution of Chen and his sons.

sentences.zh: 會延稔先至，琛等即執斬之，遣二子送延稔首啟世祖曰：「劉誕倡狂，遂構釁逆，凡在含齒，莫不駭惋，臣等預荷國恩，特百常憤。

translations.literal: It happened that Yannian arrived first; Chen and the others immediately seized and beheaded him, sent two sons to deliver Yannian's head, and memorialized Shizu: "Liu Dan in mad arrogance has constructed rebellion and offense; all who bear teeth, none fail to be shocked and grieved; we your subjects have long received the state's grace and are a hundredfold more enraged than ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: Yannian arrived first. Chen and his party immediately seized and beheaded him, then sent two sons bearing Yannian's head with a memorial to Shizu: "Liu Dan, in his mad arrogance, has raised rebellion. Every subject under heaven is shocked and grieved. We who have long received the state's grace are a hundred times more enraged than ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 忽以今月二十四日中獲賊誕疏，欲見邀誘。

translations.literal: Suddenly on the twenty-fourth of this month we obtained the rebel Dan's letter, wishing to see us enticed and recruited.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly, on the twenty-fourth of this month, we obtained a letter from the rebel Dan attempting to recruit us.

sentences.zh: 臣即共執錄偽使，並得誕與撫軍長史沈懷文、揚州別駕孔道存、撫軍中兵參軍孔璪、前司兵參軍孔桓之、前司空主簿張晏書，具列本郡太守王曇生。

translations.literal: We your subjects immediately together seized and recorded the false envoy, and also obtained Dan's letters to the Pacifying Army Chief Clerk Shen Huaiwen, Yangzhou Vice Director Kong Daocun, Pacifying Army Middle Troops Officer Kong Zuan, former Troops Officer Kong Huanzhi, and former Chief Minister Registrar Zhang Yan, fully listing the governor of this commandery, Wang Tansheng.
translations.idiomatic: We immediately seized the false envoy and also obtained letters from Dan to Shen Huaiwen, Chief Clerk of the Pacifying Army, Kong Daocun, Vice Director of Yangzhou, Kong Zuan, Middle Troops Officer of the Pacifying Army, Kong Huanzhi, former Troops Officer, and Zhang Yan, former registrar to the Chief Minister—letters that also named Wang Tansheng, governor of this commandery.

sentences.zh: 臣即日便應星馳歸骨輦轂，臣母年老，身在侍養，輒遣息寶素、寶先束骸詣闕。」

translations.literal: We your subjects that very day ought to have rushed like stars to return our bones to the imperial carriage; our mother is old and we are in attendance to nourish her, so we hastily send our sons Baosu and Baoxian bound in bonds to the palace gate."
translations.idiomatic: We should have rushed to the capital that very day, but our mother is elderly and we are attending her at home. We therefore send our sons Baosu and Baoxian bound, to present themselves at the palace gate."

sentences.zh: 世祖所遣誅琛使其日亦至，僅而獲免。

translations.literal: The envoy Shizu had sent to execute Chen arrived that same day; he barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The executioner Shizu had dispatched arrived that same day. Chen narrowly escaped death.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，召琛出，以為西陽王子尚撫軍司馬，牧為撫軍中兵參軍。

translations.literal: The emperor commended him, summoned Chen forth, and made him Pacifying Army Staff Officer to Prince of Xiyang Zishang; Mu was made Pacifying Army Middle Troops Officer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him, summoned Chen to court, and appointed him Pacifying Army Staff Officer to Prince Zishang of Xiyang. Mu was appointed Middle Troops Officer on the same staff.

sentences.zh: 琛母孔氏，時年百餘歲。

translations.literal: Chen's mother, the Kong clan, was at the time over one hundred years old.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's mother, of the Kong clan, was at the time more than one hundred years old.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝隆安初，琅邪王廞于吳中為亂，以女為貞烈將軍，悉以女人為官屬，以孔氏為司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longan under Emperor An of Jin, Prince of Langye Yin raised disorder in Wu and made his daughter General of Chaste Valor, appointing women entirely as officials, and made the Kong clan his Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longan era under Emperor An of Jin, Prince Yin of Langye raised a rebellion in Wu. He made his daughter General of Chaste Valor, appointed only women as officials, and made Lady Kong his Staff Officer.

sentences.zh: 及孫恩亂後，東土饑荒，人相食，孔氏散家糧以賑邑裏，得活者甚眾，生子皆以孔為名焉。

translations.literal: After Sun En's disorders, the eastern lands suffered famine and people ate one another; the Kong clan distributed the household grain to relieve the district, and very many were kept alive; those born thereafter all took Kong as their name.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun En's rebellion the eastern lands were stricken with famine and people resorted to cannibalism. Lady Kong distributed her household grain to feed the neighborhood, saving a great many lives. Children born thereafter were often given the name Kong in her honor.

sentences.zh: 琛仍為吳興太守。

translations.literal: Chen again served as governor of Wuxing commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was again appointed governor of Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 明年，坐郡民多翦錢及盜鑄，免官。

translations.literal: The next year, on the charge that the commandery's people extensively clipped coin and illicitly cast it, he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was dismissed from office because the people of his commandery had extensively clipped coins and engaged in illicit casting.

sentences.zh: 六年，起為大司農，都官尚書，新安王子鸞北中郎司馬、東海太守、行南徐州事，隨府轉撫軍司馬，太守如故。

translations.literal: In year six he was recalled as Director of the Grand Granary and Minister of the Capital Crimes section, Northern Central Staff Officer to Prince Luan of Xin'an, governor of Donghai and acting in South Xuzhou affairs; following the prince's household he was transferred to Pacifying Army Staff Officer, his governorship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was recalled as Director of the Grand Granary and Minister of the Capital Crimes section, and appointed Northern Central Staff Officer to Prince Luan of Xin'an, governor of Donghai, with charge of South Xuzhou affairs. When the prince's establishment moved, he became Pacifying Army Staff Officer while retaining his governorship.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝即位，複為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Former Emperor acceded, Chen was again made governor of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Former Emperor came to the throne, Chen was again appointed governor of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始初，與四方同反，兵敗，奉母奔會稽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi under Emperor Taizong, he joined the four quarters in rebellion; his troops were defeated and he fled with his mother to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taishi era under Emperor Taizong, he joined the rebellions across the realm. When his forces were defeated he fled with his mother to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 台軍既至，歸降。

translations.literal: When the imperial army arrived, he submitted and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army arrived, he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 寶素與琛相失，自殺。

translations.literal: Baosu and Chen had fallen out; he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Baosu had fallen out with Chen and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 琛尋丁母憂，服闋，起為員外常侍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: Chen soon entered mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended he was recalled as Supernumerary Regular Attendant and Grandee Without Specific Duties.
translations.idiomatic: Chen soon entered mourning for his mother. When the mourning period ended he was recalled as Supernumerary Regular Attendant and Grandee Without Specific Duties.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽三年，卒，時年八十六。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanhui under the Later Deposed Emperor he died, at age eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanhui under the Later Deposed Emperor he died, at the age of eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 寶先大明中為尚書水部郎。

translations.literal: During Daming, Baoxian served as Secretariat Officer in the Water Works section.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daming era Baoxian served as an officer in the Secretariat's Water Works section.

sentences.zh: 先是，琛為左丞荀萬秋所劾，及寶先為郎，萬秋猶在職，自陳不拜。

translations.literal: Previously Chen had been impeached by Left Vice Director Xun Wanqiu; when Baoxian became an officer Wanqiu was still in post, and Baoxian declared himself unwilling to accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chen had been impeached by Left Vice Director Xun Wanqiu. When Baoxian was appointed an officer, Wanqiu was still in that post, and Baoxian declared that he would not accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 世祖詔曰：「敕違糾慢，憲司之職，若理有不公，自當更有厘正。

translations.literal: Shizu issued an edict: "To admonish against violations and correct negligence is the duty of the censorate; if the reasoning is unjust, there should naturally be further rectification.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu issued an edict: "To admonish against violations and correct negligence is the duty of the censorate. If the reasoning is unjust, there should naturally be further rectification.

sentences.zh: 而自頃刻無輕重，輒致私絕。

translations.literal: Yet recently, without regard for severity, people repeatedly break off relations for private reasons.
translations.idiomatic: Yet recently, without regard for the severity of the offense, people have repeatedly cut off relations for private reasons.

sentences.zh: 此風難長，主者嚴為其科。

translations.literal: This practice must not be allowed to spread; the responsible officials should strictly enforce the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: This practice must not be allowed to spread. The responsible officials should strictly enforce the statutes.

sentences.zh: 寶先蓋依附世准，不足問。」

translations.literal: Baoxian merely followed the standards of his generation and is not worth pursuing."
translations.idiomatic: Baoxian merely followed the standards of his generation and is not worth pursuing further."

sentences.zh: 顧覬之，字偉仁，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Gu Jizhi, style name Weiren, was a man of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Jizhi, whose style was Weiren, came from Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖謙，字公讓，晉平原內史陸機姊夫。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Qian, style name Gongrang, was brother-in-law to Lu Ji, Jin Interior Governor of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Qian, whose style was Gongrang, was the brother-in-law of Lu Ji, Interior Governor of Pingyuan under Jin.

sentences.zh: 祖崇，大司農。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chong was Director of the Grand Granary.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chong had served as Director of the Grand Granary.

sentences.zh: 父黃老，司徒左西掾。

translations.literal: His father Huanglao was Left Western Aide to the Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huanglao had served as Left Western Aide to the Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 覬之初為郡主簿。

translations.literal: Jizhi first served as commandery chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi began his career as chief clerk of his commandery.

sentences.zh: 謝晦為荊州，以為南蠻功曹，仍為晦衛軍參軍。

translations.literal: When Xie Hui held Jingzhou, he made him Merit Officer for the Southern Man and then staff officer on Hui's Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Hui was posted to Jingzhou, he appointed Jizhi Merit Officer for the Southern Man and then staff officer on Hui's Guard Army.

sentences.zh: 晦愛其雅素，深相知待。

translations.literal: Hui loved his refined simplicity and treated him with deep mutual regard.
translations.idiomatic: Hui admired his refined simplicity and treated him with deep trust and regard.

sentences.zh: 王弘辟為揚州主簿，仍為弘衛軍參軍，鹽官令，衡陽王義季右軍主簿，尚書都官郎，護軍司馬。

translations.literal: Wang Hong recruited him as Yangzhou chief clerk, then as Hong's Guard Army staff officer, magistrate of Yanguan, Right Army chief clerk to Prince of Hengyang Yiji, Secretariat Officer in the Capital Crimes section, and Protecting Army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong recruited him as chief clerk of Yangzhou, then as staff officer on Hong's Guard Army, magistrate of Yanguan, Right Army chief clerk to Prince Yiji of Hengyang, an officer in the Secretariat's capital-crimes section, and Protecting Army marshal.

sentences.zh: 時大將軍彭城王義康秉權，殷、劉之隙已著，覬之不欲與殷景仁久接事，乃辭腳疾自免歸。

translations.literal: At the time the Grand General, Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, held power; the rift between Yin and Liu was already manifest; Jizhi did not wish to serve long with Yin Jingren and so pleaded foot ailment to resign and return home.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Grand General Prince Yikang of Pengcheng held power, and the rift between Yin Jingren and Liu Yilong was already open. Jizhi did not wish to serve alongside Yin Jingren and pleaded a foot ailment to resign and return home.

sentences.zh: 在家每夜常于床上行腳，家人竊異之，而莫曉其意。

translations.literal: At home each night he would often walk his feet upon the bed; the household privately found it strange but none understood his intent.
translations.idiomatic: At home he would walk about on his bed each night. His family found this strange but none understood his purpose.

sentences.zh: 後義康徙廢，朝廷多以異同受禍。

translations.literal: Later Yikang was demoted and disgraced; many at court suffered calamity for their affiliations.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Yikang was demoted and disgraced, many at court suffered ruin for their political affiliations.

sentences.zh: 復為東遷、山陰令。

translations.literal: He again served as magistrate of Dongqian and Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as magistrate of Dongqian and Shanyin in succession.

sentences.zh: 山陰民戶三萬，海內劇邑，前後官長，晝夜不得休，事猶不舉。

translations.literal: Shanyin had thirty thousand households, a commandery of the greatest difficulty within the realm; successive magistrates could not rest day or night, yet affairs still went unaccomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyin had thirty thousand households and was among the most demanding counties in the realm. Successive magistrates worked day and night without rest, yet still could not keep up with their duties.

sentences.zh: 覬之理繁以約，縣用無事，晝日垂簾，門階閑寂。

translations.literal: Jizhi governed complexity through simplicity; the county had no troubles; by day he let the curtain hang and the gate and steps were quiet and still.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi governed complexity through simplicity. The county ran without incident; by day he let the curtain hang down, and his gate and courtyard stood quiet and still.

sentences.zh: 自宋世為山陰，務簡而績修，莫能尚也。

translations.literal: From the Song era as magistrate of Shanyin, his affairs were simple yet his achievements well ordered—none could surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: From the Song period onward, no magistrate of Shanyin had matched his combination of simple administration and well-ordered achievement.

sentences.zh: 還為揚州治中從事史，廣陵王誕、廬陵王紹北中郎左司馬，揚州別駕從事史，尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: He returned as Yangzhou Senior Clerk, Northern Central Left Staff Officer to Princes of Guangling Dan and of Luling Shao, Yangzhou Vice Director, and Secretariat Officer in the Civil Service section.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to serve as Senior Clerk of Yangzhou, Northern Central Left Staff Officer to Princes Dan of Guangling and Shao of Luling, Vice Director of Yangzhou, and an officer in the Secretariat's civil-service section.

sentences.zh: 嘗于太祖坐論江左人物，言及顧榮，袁淑謂覬之曰：「卿南人怯懦，豈辦作賊。」

translations.literal: Once at a gathering of Taizu discussing figures of the Jiang left, when Gu Rong was mentioned Yuan Shu said to Jizhi: "You southerners are timid and weak—how could you manage to be rebels?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, at a gathering of Taizu discussing figures of the Jiang left, Gu Rong's name came up. Yuan Shu said to Jizhi, "You southerners are timid and weak—how could you ever manage to be rebels?"

sentences.zh: 覬之正色曰：「卿乃複以忠義笑人！」

translations.literal: Jizhi with stern countenance said: "You would mock a man for his loyalty and righteousness!"
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi replied with a stern face, "You would mock a man for his loyalty and righteousness!"

sentences.zh: 淑有愧色。

translations.literal: Shu showed a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Shu looked ashamed.

sentences.zh: 時沛郡相縣唐賜往比村硃起母彭家飲酒還，因得病，吐蠱蟲十餘枚。

translations.literal: At the time Tang Ci of Xiang county in Pei commandery went to drink at the home of Zhu Qi's mother Peng in a neighboring village; on returning he fell ill and vomited more than ten gu worms.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Tang Ci of Xiang county in Pei commandery had gone to drink at the home of Zhu Qi's mother, Lady Peng, in a neighboring village. On his return he fell ill and vomited more than ten gu worms.

sentences.zh: 臨死語妻張，死後刳腹出病。

translations.literal: On the verge of death he told his wife Zhang that after death she should cut open his belly to bring out the disease.
translations.idiomatic: On the verge of death he told his wife Zhang that after he died she should cut open his belly to remove the disease.

sentences.zh: 後張手自破視，五藏悉糜碎。

translations.literal: Later Zhang with her own hands broke him open to look; all five viscera were utterly pulverized.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang opened his body with her own hands and found all five viscera utterly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 郡縣以張忍行刳剖，賜子副又不禁駐，事起赦前，法不能決。

translations.literal: The commandery and county, because Zhang had endured performing the cutting and dissection and Ci's son Fu had not restrained or halted her, and because the matter arose before an amnesty so the law could not decide it.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery and county authorities noted that Zhang had carried out the dissection, that Ci's son Fu had not restrained her, and that the matter had arisen before a general amnesty, so the law could not settle the case.

sentences.zh: 律傷死人，四歲刑；

translations.literal: The statutes: injuring a dead person, four years' punishment;
translations.idiomatic: The statutes prescribed four years' punishment for injuring a dead person;

sentences.zh: 妻傷夫，五歲刑；

translations.literal: a wife injuring her husband, five years' punishment;
translations.idiomatic: five years for a wife injuring her husband;

sentences.zh: 子不孝父母，棄市，並非科例。

translations.literal: a son not filial to parents, execution at the market—all were not statutory categories.
translations.idiomatic: and execution at the market for a son's lack of filial piety—but none of these fit the case as written.

sentences.zh: 三公郎劉勰議：「賜妻痛往遵言，兒識謝及理，考事原心，非存忍害，謂宜哀矜。」

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Three Excellencies Liu Xie argued: "Ci's wife in grief followed his last words; the son knew to apologize and understood the reasoning; examining the matter by the original intent, there was no intent to harm—it should be treated with compassion."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xie, Gentleman of the Three Excellencies, argued: "Ci's wife in her grief followed his last words; the son understood and apologized. Examining the matter by its original intent, there was no wish to harm. The court should show compassion."

sentences.zh: 覬之議曰：「法移路屍，猶為不道，況在妻子，而忍行凡人所不行。

translations.literal: Jizhi argued: "By law, even moving a corpse on the road is deemed unnatural conduct; how much more so for wife and son to endure doing what ordinary people cannot do.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi argued: "By law, even moving a corpse found on the road counts as unnatural conduct. How much more so when wife and son perform what ordinary people could not bear to do.

sentences.zh: 不宜曲通小情，當以大理為斷，謂副為不孝，張同不道。」

translations.literal: One should not bend the great principle to accommodate small feeling; judgment should be made by the great standard—I hold Fu guilty of unfilial conduct and Zhang equally of unnatural conduct."
translations.idiomatic: One should not bend the great principle to accommodate private feeling. Judgment should follow the greater standard: Fu is guilty of unfilial conduct, and Zhang of unnatural conduct as well."

sentences.zh: 詔如覬之議。

translations.literal: The edict followed Jizhi's argument.
translations.idiomatic: The edict followed Jizhi's argument.

sentences.zh: 加左軍將軍，出為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General of the Left Army and sent out as governor of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Left Army and sent out as governor of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 八年，複為吏部尚書，加給事中，未拜，欲以為會稽，不果。

translations.literal: In year eight he was again made Minister of the Civil Service, with addition of Attendant Within the Gates; before he could accept the appointment he was intended for Kuaiji but it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was again appointed Minister of the Civil Service with the additional title Attendant Within the Gates. Before he could take up the post he was slated for Kuaiji, but the appointment did not materialize.

sentences.zh: 還為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: He returned as governor of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to serve as governor of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 幸臣戴法興權傾人主，而覬之未嘗降意。

translations.literal: The favored minister Dai Faxing's power tilted toward overshadowing the sovereign, yet Jizhi never lowered his bearing toward him.
translations.idiomatic: The favored minister Dai Faxing wielded power that overshadowed the throne itself, yet Jizhi never deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 左光祿大夫蔡興宗與覬之善，嫌其風節過峻。

translations.literal: Left Grandee of the Imperial Household Cai Xingzong was on good terms with Jizhi but disliked that his moral bearing was too severe.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xingzong, Left Grandee of the Imperial Household, was on good terms with Jizhi but worried that his moral bearing was too severe.

sentences.zh: 覬之曰：「辛毗有雲：孫、劉不過使吾不為三公耳！」

translations.literal: Jizhi said: "Xin Pi once said: Sun and Liu could do no more than keep me from becoming one of the Three Excellencies!"
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi said, "Xin Pi once remarked that Sun and Liu could do no more than keep me from becoming one of the Three Excellencies!"

sentences.zh: 及世祖晏駕，法興遂以覬之為光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。

translations.literal: When Shizu passed away, Faxing then made Jizhi Grandee of the Imperial Household, with addition of golden seal and purple cord.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu died, Faxing appointed Jizhi Grandee of the Imperial Household with a golden seal and purple cord.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始初，四方同反，覬之家尋陽，尋陽王子房加以位號，覬之不受，曰：「禮年六十不服戎，以其筋力衰謝，非複軍旅之日，況年將八十，殘生無幾，守盡家門，不敢聞命。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi under Taizong, when the four quarters rebelled together, Jizhi's household was at Xunyang; Prince Zifang of Xunyang offered him rank and title; Jizhi did not accept, saying: "By ritual, at sixty one does not take up arms, for one's sinews and strength have declined and the days of campaigning are past; how much more at nearly eighty, with but a remnant of life remaining—I shall guard my household to the end and dare not heed the command."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taishi era under Emperor Taizong, when rebellions broke out across the realm, Jizhi was at home in Xunyang. Prince Zifang of Xunyang offered him rank and title, but Jizhi refused, saying, "By ritual, at sixty one does not take up arms, for one's strength has declined and the days of campaigning are past. At nearly eighty, with only a remnant of life remaining, I shall guard my household to the end and dare not accept your command."

sentences.zh: 孔覬等不能奪。

translations.literal: Kong Yi and the others could not change his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yi and the others could not change his mind.

sentences.zh: 時普天叛逆，莫或自免，唯覬之心跡清全，獨無所與。

translations.literal: At the time all under heaven rebelled and none could escape involvement; only Jizhi's mind and conduct were pure and complete, sharing in nothing.
translations.idiomatic: At the time rebellion swept the realm and scarcely anyone escaped involvement. Only Jizhi's conduct remained pure and untouched.

sentences.zh: 太宗甚嘉之，東土既平，以為左將軍、吳郡太守，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Taizong greatly commended him; when the eastern lands were pacified he was made General of the Left, governor of Wu commandery, with addition of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong greatly commended him. When the eastern lands were pacified he was appointed General of the Left, governor of Wu commandery, and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年，複為湘州刺史，常侍、將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi he was again made governor of Xiangzhou; Regular Attendant and general's rank as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taishi he was again appointed governor of Xiangzhou, retaining his titles as Regular Attendant and general.

sentences.zh: 三年卒，時年七十六。

translations.literal: In year three he died, at age seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died, at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 追贈鎮軍將軍，常侍、刺史如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the Army; Regular Attendant and provincial governor as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the rank of General Who Pacifies the Army, retaining his titles as Regular Attendant and provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 諡曰簡子。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Succinct Master.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Succinct Master.

sentences.zh: 覬之家門雍睦，為州鄉所重。

translations.literal: Jizhi's household was harmonious and esteemed by the commandery and district.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi's household was harmonious and held in high esteem throughout the commandery and district.

sentences.zh: 五子：約、緝、綽、縝、緄。

translations.literal: Five sons: Yue, Ji, Chuo, Zhen, and Gun.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Yue, Ji, Chuo, Zhen, and Gun.

sentences.zh: 綽私財甚豐，鄉里士庶多負其責，覬之每禁之，不能止。

translations.literal: Chuo's private wealth was very abundant; many gentry and commoners of the district owed him debts; Jizhi repeatedly forbade this but could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo had amassed considerable private wealth, and many gentry and commoners of the district owed him money. Jizhi repeatedly forbade such lending but could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 及後為吳郡，誘綽曰：「我常不許汝出責，定思貧薄亦不可居。

translations.literal: When later he became governor of Wu commandery, he coaxed Chuo, saying: "I have always forbidden you to lend out debts; surely you have considered that poverty is also unbearable.
translations.idiomatic: When he later became governor of Wu commandery, he coaxed Chuo, saying, "I have always forbidden you to lend money. You must have realized that poverty is unbearable as well.

sentences.zh: 民間與汝交關有幾許不盡，及我在郡，為汝督之。

translations.literal: How many of the dealings between the people and you remain unsettled? While I am in the commandery I shall press collection for you.
translations.idiomatic: How many of your outstanding debts remain unsettled? While I am in the commandery I shall collect them for you.

sentences.zh: 將來豈可得。

translations.literal: In the future how could they be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Once I am gone, how will you ever collect them?

sentences.zh: 凡諸券書皆何在？」

translations.literal: Where are all the bond documents?"
translations.idiomatic: Where are all the loan documents?"

sentences.zh: 綽大喜，悉出諸文券一大廚與覬之，覬之悉焚燒，宣語遠近：「負三郎責，皆不須還，凡券書悉燒之矣。」

translations.literal: Chuo was greatly pleased and brought out all the written bonds from a great cupboard to Jizhi; Jizhi burned them all and proclaimed to near and far: "Debts owed to the Third Son need not be repaid—all bond documents have been burned."
translations.idiomatic: Chuo was delighted and brought out all the loan documents from a large cupboard. Jizhi burned every one of them and proclaimed throughout the district, "Debts owed to the Third Son need not be repaid—all loan documents have been burned."

sentences.zh: 綽懊歎彌日。

translations.literal: Chuo grieved and sighed for a full day.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo grieved and sighed for an entire day.

sentences.zh: 覬之常謂秉命有定分，非智力所移，唯應恭己守道，信天任運，而暗者不達，妄求僥倖，徒虧雅道，無關得喪。

translations.literal: Jizhi often said that allotted fate has a fixed allotment, not something intelligence or strength can shift; one should only respectfully keep to the Way, trust Heaven and accept one's lot—yet the obtuse do not comprehend and vainly seek good fortune, merely harming the refined Way with no bearing on gain or loss.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi often said that allotted fate has a fixed portion that intelligence and strength cannot alter. One should respectfully keep to the Way, trust Heaven, and accept one's lot. The obtuse fail to understand this and vainly seek good fortune, harming the refined Way without affecting gain or loss in the least.

sentences.zh: 乃以其意命弟子願著《定命論》，其辭曰：

translations.literal: He therefore had his disciple Yuan compose the "Treatise on Fixed Fate" according to his meaning; its words say:
translations.idiomatic: He therefore had his disciple Yuan compose the Treatise on Fixed Fate according to his views. Its text reads:

sentences.zh: 仲尼雲：「道之將行，命也；

translations.literal: Zhongni said: "When the Way is about to be practiced, it is fate;
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "When the Way is about to prevail, that is fate;

sentences.zh: 道之將廢，命也。」

translations.literal: when the Way is about to fall into disuse, it is fate."
translations.idiomatic: when the Way is about to fall into disuse, that is fate as well."

sentences.zh: 丘明又稱：「天之所支不可壞，天之所壞不可支。」

translations.literal: Qiuming also said: "What Heaven supports cannot be destroyed; what Heaven destroys cannot be supported."
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Qiuming also wrote, "What Heaven supports cannot be destroyed; what Heaven destroys cannot be propped up."

sentences.zh: 卜商亦曰：「死生有命，富貴在天。」

translations.literal: Bushang also said: "Life and death have allotment; wealth and honor lie with Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Zixia also said, "Life and death are allotted; wealth and honor lie with Heaven."

sentences.zh: 孟軻則以不遇魯侯為辭。

translations.literal: Meng Ke took not meeting the Marquis of Lu as his explanation.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius explained his failure to meet the Marquis of Lu in the same terms.

sentences.zh: 斯則運命奇偶，生數離合，有自來矣。

translations.literal: Thus the odd and even of fortune's turns, the joining and parting of life's numbers, have had their origin from of old.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the alternations of fortune, the joining and parting of life's allotments, have had their origin from the beginning.

sentences.zh: 馬遷、劉向、揚雄、班固之徒，著書立言，鹹以為首，世之論者，多有不同。

translations.literal: Sima Qian, Liu Xiang, Yang Xiong, Ban Gu and the like, in composing books and establishing discourse, all took this as foremost; yet commentators of the age have often differed.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian, Liu Xiang, Yang Xiong, Ban Gu, and others, in their writings, all placed this question foremost—yet commentators of later ages have often disagreed.

sentences.zh: 嘗試申之曰：

translations.literal: I shall attempt to set it forth, saying:
translations.idiomatic: I shall attempt to set forth my view as follows:

sentences.zh: 夫生之資氣，清濁異原；

translations.literal: Now the endowment of life draws on qi—clear and turbid have different sources;
translations.idiomatic: Life draws on qi, whose clear and turbid sources differ;

sentences.zh: 命之稟數，盈虛乖致。

translations.literal: fate's received numbers, fullness and emptiness diverge in their arrival.
translations.idiomatic: and fate's allotted numbers arrive in fullness or emptiness according to their own pattern.

sentences.zh: 是以心貌詭貿，性運舛殊，故有邪正昏明之差，修夭榮枯之序，皆理定於萬古之前，事征於千代之外，沖神寂鑒，一以貫之。

translations.literal: Therefore mind and appearance are strangely diverse, nature and fortune oddly distinct; hence the differences of perverse and upright, dim and bright, the sequence of long life and early death, glory and withering—all principle was fixed before ten thousand ages, affairs verified beyond a thousand generations; the subtle spirit in silent contemplation comprehends them with one thread running through.
translations.idiomatic: Hence mind and appearance vary strangely, and nature and fortune diverge. The differences between the perverse and the upright, the dim and the bright, the sequence of long life and early death, glory and decline—all were fixed in principle before the beginning of time and are verified across a thousand generations. The subtle spirit perceives them in silent unity.

sentences.zh: 至乃卜相末技，巫史賤術，猶能豫題興亡，逆表成敗。

translations.literal: Even the petty skills of divination and physiognomy, the base arts of shamans and recorders, can still foretell rise and fall in advance and set forth success and failure in reverse.
translations.idiomatic: Even the petty arts of divination and physiognomy, the low crafts of shamans and clerks, can foretell rise and fall in advance and read success and failure before they occur.

sentences.zh: 禍福指期，識照不能徙；

translations.literal: When fortune and calamity point to their term, knowledge and insight cannot shift them;
translations.idiomatic: When fortune and calamity are fixed to their term, knowledge and insight cannot alter them;

sentences.zh: 吉凶素著，威衛不能防。

translations.literal: when good and ill are plainly manifest, authority and guards cannot prevent them.
translations.idiomatic: when good and ill fortune are plainly ordained, authority and guards cannot forestall them.

sentences.zh: 若夏氓宅生於帝宮，豈蠲殘傷之祟；

translations.literal: If a Xia commoner were born dwelling in the imperial palace, how could he escape the affliction of mutilation and harm;
translations.idiomatic: If a commoner of Xia had been born in the imperial palace, he could not have escaped the affliction of mutilation;

sentences.zh: 漢臣衍貨于天府，寧免喂斃之魂。

translations.literal: if a Han minister traded goods in the celestial treasury, could he avoid the soul of one fed to death?
translations.idiomatic: if a minister of Han had hoarded goods in the imperial storehouse, he could not have escaped a violent end.

sentences.zh: 且又善惡之理雖詳，而禍福之驗常昧；

translations.literal: Moreover, though the principle of good and evil is detailed, the verification of fortune and calamity is often obscure;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though the principle of good and evil is clear in theory, the verification of fortune and calamity is often obscure;

sentences.zh: 逆順之體誠分，而吉凶之效常隱。

translations.literal: the substance of rebellion and obedience is truly divided, yet the effect of good and ill fortune is often hidden.
translations.idiomatic: the substance of rebellion and obedience is truly distinct, yet the outcome of good and ill fortune is often hidden.

sentences.zh: 智絡天地，猶罹沈牖之災；

translations.literal: Wisdom spanning Heaven and Earth still suffers the calamity of drowning in a deep window-well;
translations.idiomatic: Wisdom spanning Heaven and Earth still suffers calamity;

sentences.zh: 明照日月，必嬰深匡之難。

translations.literal: brightness illuminating sun and moon must encounter the hardship of a deep pit.
translations.idiomatic: brightness illuminating sun and moon still meets with disaster in a deep pit.

sentences.zh: 增信積德，離患於長飢；

translations.literal: Increasing faith and accumulating virtue do not remove one from long famine;
translations.idiomatic: Increasing faith and accumulating virtue do not spare one from long famine;

sentences.zh: 席義枕仁，徼禍於促算。

translations.literal: resting on righteousness and pillowing benevolence still invite calamity in a shortened lifespan.
translations.idiomatic: resting on righteousness and pillowing benevolence still invite calamity within a shortened lifespan.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 理運苟其必至，聖明其猶病諸。

translations.literal: If principle and fortune must arrive as ordained, even the sage and enlightened still suffer from them.
translations.idiomatic: If principle and fortune must arrive as ordained, even the sage and the enlightened still suffer from them.

sentences.zh: 況乃蕞跡流惑之徒，投心顓蒙之域，而欲役慮以揣利害，策情以算窮通，其為重傷，豈不惑甚。

translations.literal: How much more those petty traces adrift in confusion, casting their hearts into the realm of obstinate ignorance, yet wishing to deploy thought to gauge benefit and harm, deploy feeling to calculate success and failure—their self-inflicted wounds, are they not profoundly deluded?
translations.idiomatic: How much more those petty souls adrift in confusion, casting their hearts into obstinate ignorance, yet trying to deploy thought to gauge benefit and harm and deploy feeling to calculate success and failure—the wounds they inflict on themselves are profound indeed, and their delusion extreme.

sentences.zh: 是以通人君子，閑泰其神，沖緩其度，不矯俗以延聲，不依世以期榮。

translations.literal: Therefore the penetrating man and the gentleman ease their spirits, moderate their measure, do not bend custom to prolong reputation, do not rely on the age to expect glory.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the penetrating man and the gentleman ease their spirits and moderate their pace. They do not bend to custom to prolong their reputation, nor rely on the age to expect glory.

sentences.zh: 審乎無假，自求多福，榮辱修夭，夫何為哉！

translations.literal: Discerning that there is no falsehood, they seek much blessing for themselves—glory and shame, long life and early death, what are they to such a one!
translations.idiomatic: Discerning that nothing is false, they seek blessing for themselves. Glory and shame, long life and early death—what can these matter to such a one!

sentences.zh: 問曰：夫《書》稱惠迪貽吉，《易》載履信逢祐，前哲餘議，亦以將迎有會，淪塞無兆，宣攝有方，夭閼無命。

translations.literal: A question says: The Documents praise following the Way to leave blessing; the Changes record keeping faith to meet assistance; the remaining discourse of former sages also holds that meeting has its occasion, obstruction has no omen, regulation has its method, and premature blocking has no fate.
translations.idiomatic: A questioner asks: The Documents praise following the Way to leave blessing behind; the Changes record that keeping faith meets with divine aid; and former sages have also held that meeting has its occasion, obstruction has no omen, regulation has its method, and premature blocking has no relation to fate.

sentences.zh: 善游銷魂于深梁，工騎燼生於曠野，明珠招駭於暗至，蟠木取悅于先容。

translations.literal: The skilled swimmer loses his soul in a deep beam; the skilled rider's embers are born in open wilds; a bright pearl draws alarm in dark arrival; a coiled tree wins favor through prior countenance.
translations.idiomatic: The skilled swimmer loses his soul in a deep beam; the skilled rider's mount founders in open wilds; a bright pearl draws danger in the dark; a gnarled tree wins favor through prior cultivation.

sentences.zh: 是以罕、樂以陽施長世；

translations.literal: Thus Han and Yue, through yang-bestowal, prolonged their generations;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the states of Han and Yue, through active benevolence openly bestowed, endured for generations;

sentences.zh: 景、惠以陰德遐紀。

translations.literal: Jing and Hui, through yin-virtue, enjoyed distant ages.
translations.idiomatic: Kings Jing and Hui of Zhou, through hidden virtue, enjoyed reigns of long duration.

sentences.zh: 彭、竇以繕衛延命；

translations.literal: Peng and Dou, through tending and guarding, extended life;
translations.idiomatic: Pengzu and Old Dou, through tending and guarding their lives, extended their allotted spans;

sentences.zh: 盈、忌以荒湎促齡。

translations.literal: Ying and Ji, through reckless drunkenness, shortened their years.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhou Xin and Li Ji, through reckless debauchery and drink, shortened their years.

sentences.zh: 陳、張稱台鼎之崇；

translations.literal: Chen and Zhang attained the loftiness of the tripod-and-cauldron rank;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ping and Zhang Liang attained the eminence of the highest ministerial rank;

sentences.zh: 嚴、辛衍宰司之盛。

translations.literal: Yan and Xin spread the grandeur of chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun and Xin Ping spread the grandeur of chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 若乃遊惡蹈凶，處逆踐禍，宣昭史策，易以研正。

translations.literal: As for those who wandered in evil and trod through calamity, who dwelt in rebellion and stepped on disaster—the historical records proclaim them clearly, and their cases are easily examined and set right.
translations.idiomatic: As for those who wandered in evil and trod through calamity, who dwelt in rebellion and stepped on disaster—the historical records proclaim them clearly, and their cases are easily examined and set right.

sentences.zh: 至如神仙所序，天竺所書，事雖難征，理未易詰，留滯傾光，思聞通裁。

translations.literal: But as for what immortals have set down and what India has recorded—though the facts are hard to verify, the principles are not easily refuted; I linger here, inclined to yield, and would hear comprehensive judgment.
translations.idiomatic: But as for what immortals have set down and what India has recorded—though the facts are hard to verify, the principles are not easily refuted. I linger here, inclined to yield, and would hear your comprehensive judgment.

sentences.zh: 對曰：子可謂扶繩而辨，循刻而議。

translations.literal: The reply came: You may be said to argue by holding a rope and to debate by following a marking on the sundial.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: You may be said to argue by holding the rope of the argument and to debate by following the sundial's shadow—your reasoning is exacting indeed.

sentences.zh: 若乃宣攝有方，豈非吉運所屬；

translations.literal: As for regulating and governing with proper method—is that not what fortunate destiny belongs to?
translations.idiomatic: As for regulating and governing with proper method—is that not the province of fortunate destiny?

sentences.zh: 將迎有會，實亦凶數自挻。

translations.literal: That meeting has its occasion is true; yet ill-fated numbers also extend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: That meeting has its occasion is true; yet ill-fated numbers also extend themselves of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 若夫陽施陰德，長世遐年，揆厥所原，孰往非命。

translations.literal: As for yang-bestowal and yin-virtue, long generations and distant years—when one traces them to their origin, where does anything go that is not fate?
translations.idiomatic: As for active benevolence and hidden virtue, long generations and distant years—when one traces them to their origin, where does anything go that is not fate?

sentences.zh: 研復來旨，讎校往說，起予惟商，未識所異。

translations.literal: I have studied your latest meaning and collated it with earlier discourse; you enlighten me—I can discuss with you, yet I do not see where we differ.
translations.idiomatic: I have studied your latest meaning and collated it with earlier discourse. You enlighten me—I can discuss with you, yet I do not see where we differ.

sentences.zh: 資生稟運，參差萬殊，逆順吉凶，理數不一。

translations.literal: The endowment of life and received fortune vary among ten thousand differences; rebellion and obedience, good and ill, follow principles and numbers that are not one.
translations.idiomatic: The endowment of life and received fortune vary among ten thousand differences; rebellion and obedience, good and ill, follow principles and numbers that are not one.

sentences.zh: 原夫餐椒非養生之術，咀劍豈衛性之經。

translations.literal: For eating pepper is not a method of nourishing life, and chewing swords is hardly a canon for guarding one's nature.
translations.idiomatic: For eating pepper is not a method of nourishing life, and chewing swords is hardly a canon for guarding one's nature.

sentences.zh: 命之所延，人肉其骨，而含嚼膏粱，時或嬰患。

translations.literal: Where fate extends life, one eats human flesh to the bone—yet those who chew rich grains still sometimes contract illness.
translations.idiomatic: Where fate extends life, one may eat human flesh to the bone—yet those who chew rich grains still sometimes contract illness.

sentences.zh: 深澗乖徼寵之津，空谷絕探榮之轍，運之所集，物稊其枯，而俯仰竿牘，終然離沮。

translations.literal: Deep ravines miss the ford of favor; empty valleys cut off tracks of seeking glory—where fortune gathers, things wither to dryness, while those who bow and rise with brush and document still end in separation and dejection.
