translations.idiomatic: Deep ravines lack paths to favor; empty valleys cut off tracks to glory—where fortune gathers, things wither to dryness, while those who bow and rise with brush and document still end in separation and dejection.

sentences.zh: 爾乃蹻、蹠橫行；

translations.literal: Then Bo Yi and Robber Zhi go unrestrained;
translations.idiomatic: Then Bo Yi and Robber Zhi go unrestrained;

sentences.zh: 曾、原窘步。

translations.literal: Zeng Shen and Yan Yuan walk in distress.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Shen and Yan Yuan walk in distress.

sentences.zh: 湯、周延世，詡、邑絕緒。

translations.literal: Tang and Zhou extended their generations; Xu and Yi ended their lines.
translations.idiomatic: Tang and Zhou extended their lines through generations; Xu You and Boyi ended without posterity.

sentences.zh: 吉凶征應，糾纆若茲。

translations.literal: The omens of good and ill correspond, tangled together thus.
translations.idiomatic: The omens of good and ill fortune correspond, tangled together thus.

sentences.zh: 畢萬保軀，宓賤喪領，梁野之言，豈不或妄。

translations.literal: Bi Wan preserved his body, Mi Zijian lost his head—are Liang Yi's words not perhaps mistaken?
translations.idiomatic: Bi Wan preserved his body, Mi Zijian lost his head—are Liang Yi's words not perhaps mistaken?

sentences.zh: 谷南、魯北，甘此促生；

translations.literal: South of the valley, north of Lu—they willingly accept this shortened life;
translations.idiomatic: South of the valley, north of Lu—they willingly accept this shortened span of life;

sentences.zh: 彭翁、竇叟，將以何術。

translations.literal: Old Peng, Old Dou—by what arts?
translations.idiomatic: Old Peng and Old Dou—by what arts did they do it?

sentences.zh: 晉平、趙敬，淫放已該；

translations.literal: Duke Ping of Jin and King Jing of Zhao—licentious and dissolute, already complete;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Ping of Jin and King Jing of Zhao were licentious and dissolute to the full;

sentences.zh: 漢主、魏相，奚獨傷夭。

translations.literal: The Han lord and the Wei minister—why alone die young?
translations.idiomatic: The Han emperor and the Wei minister—why did they alone die young?

sentences.zh: 同異若斯，是非孰正。

translations.literal: Similarities and differences like these—which is right and which wrong?
translations.idiomatic: Similarities and differences like these—which view is right and which wrong?

sentences.zh: 至如雷濱凝分，挫志遠圖；

translations.literal: As when at Lei Ford the streams congealed and parted, frustrating ambitions for distant achievement;
translations.idiomatic: As when at Lei Ford the streams congealed and parted, frustrating ambitions for distant achievement;

sentences.zh: 棘津陰拱，振功高世。

translations.literal: while at Jiji Ford one waited in hidden stillness and shook the age with lofty merit.
translations.idiomatic: while at Jiji Ford one waited in hidden stillness and shook the age with lofty merit.

sentences.zh: 樊生沖矯，鐫旌善之文，華子高抗，銘懲非之策，皆士衡所雲「同川而異歸」者也。

translations.literal: Fan Sheng strove upward and engraved words praising the good; Hua Zi stood high in opposition and inscribed policies warning against evil—all examples of what Lu Ji called "the same stream yet different destinations."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sheng strove upward and engraved words praising the good; Hua Zi stood high in opposition and inscribed policies warning against evil—all examples of what Lu Ji called "the same stream yet different destinations."

sentences.zh: 殊塗均致，實繁有征。

translations.literal: Different paths reach the same end—instances of this are indeed numerous and verified.
translations.idiomatic: Different paths reach the same end—instances of this are indeed numerous and verified.

sentences.zh: 即理易推，在言可略。

translations.literal: Following from principle one can easily infer; in words it may be brief.
translations.idiomatic: Following from principle one can easily infer; in words it may be brief.

sentences.zh: 昔兩都全盛，六合殷昌，霧集貴寵之閭，雲動權豪之術，鈞貿貽談，豈唯陳、張而已。

translations.literal: In former days when both capitals were in full splendor and the realm prospered, mist gathered in lanes of noble favor and clouds stirred in wards of powerful magnates—tales of equal price in trade were handed down; was it only Chen and Zhang?
translations.idiomatic: In former days when both capitals were in full splendor and the realm prospered, mist gathered in lanes of noble favor and clouds stirred in wards of powerful magnates—tales of equal standing were handed down; was it only Chen Ping and Zhang Liang?

sentences.zh: 觀夫二子，才未越眾，而此以藉榮揮價，彼獨擯景淪聲，通否之運，斷可知矣。

translations.literal: Considering these two men, their talent did not surpass the multitude, yet one rode borrowed glory to raise his price while the other alone was cast into shadow and sank in repute—the fortune of passage or obstruction can clearly be known.
translations.idiomatic: Considering these two men, their talent did not surpass the multitude, yet one rode borrowed glory to raise his price while the other alone was cast into shadow and sank in repute—the fortune of passage or obstruction can clearly be known.

sentences.zh: 嚴、辛不安時任命，而委罪亮直，亦地脈之徒歟。

translations.literal: Yan and Xin did not rest content with their allotted times and appointments, yet blamed the straight and bright—is this also the cohort of those who talk of underground veins?
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun and Xin Ping did not rest content with their allotted times and appointments, yet blamed the straight and bright—is this also the cohort of those who talk of underground veins?

sentences.zh: 若神仙所序，顯明修習，齊強燕平，厥驗未著，李覃董芬，其效安在。

translations.literal: As for what immortals set forth and bright cultivation—Qi was strong, Yan was pacified, yet their verification did not appear; Li Tan and Dong Fen—where are their effects?
translations.idiomatic: As for what immortals set forth and bright cultivation—Qi was strong, Yan was pacified, yet their verification did not appear; Li Tan and Dong Fen—where are their effects?

sentences.zh: 喬、松之侶，雲飛天居，夷、列之徒，風行水息，良由理數懸挺，實乃鐘茲景命。

translations.literal: Companions of Qiao and Song soar through clouds and dwell in heaven; followers of Boyi and Liezi move with the wind and rest upon the water—truly because principle and number stand far apart, they in fact received this splendid destiny.
translations.idiomatic: Companions of Wang Qiao and Chi Songzi soar through clouds and dwell in heaven; followers of Boyi and Liezi move with the wind and rest upon the water—truly because principle and number stand far apart, they in fact received this splendid destiny.

sentences.zh: 天竺遺文，星華方策，因造前定，果報指期，貧豪莫差，修夭無爽，有允瑣辭，無愆鄙說，統而言之，孰往非命。

translations.literal: India's transmitted texts and the star-flowered cubic charts establish prior determination; karmic retribution points to its term; poor and great are not differentiated, long life and early death are not in error; there are trustworthy petty phrases and no fault in humble discourse—unified in speech, where does anything go that is not fate?
translations.idiomatic: India's transmitted texts and the star-flowered cubic charts establish prior determination; karmic retribution points to its term; poor and great are not differentiated, long life and early death are not in error; there are trustworthy petty phrases and no fault in humble discourse—unified in speech, where does anything go that is not fate?

sentences.zh: 冥期前定，各從所歸，善惡無所矯其趨，愚智焉能殊其理。

translations.literal: Dark terms are fixed beforehand; each follows where he is bound; good and evil cannot alter their course, fool and sage—how can they differ in principle?
translations.idiomatic: Dark terms are fixed beforehand; each follows where he is bound; good and evil cannot alter their course—how can fool and sage differ in principle?

sentences.zh: 若乃得議其工，失嗤其拙，操之則栗，舍之則悲，斯固染情於近累，豈不貽誚於通識。

translations.literal: If one praises another's skill when he succeeds and mocks his clumsiness when he fails, trembles when holding it and grieves when letting go—this is surely staining feeling with nearby entanglements; does it not invite reproach from penetrating understanding?
translations.idiomatic: If one praises another's skill when he succeeds and mocks his clumsiness when he fails, trembles when holding it and grieves when letting go—this is surely staining feeling with nearby entanglements; does it not invite reproach from penetrating understanding?

sentences.zh: 問曰：清論光心，英辯溢目，求諸鄙懷，良有未盡。

translations.literal: A question says: Your lucid discourse illuminates the heart and your eloquent argument overflows the eye; sought within my humble breast, much still remains unsaid.
translations.idiomatic: The questioner asked: Your lucid discourse illuminates the heart and your eloquent argument overflows the eye; sought within my humble breast, much still remains unsaid.

sentences.zh: 若動止皆運，險易自天，理定前期，靡非暗至。

translations.literal: If every movement and rest is fortune, every hardship and ease from Heaven, principle fixed in an earlier term, nothing not arriving in darkness—
translations.idiomatic: If every movement and rest is fortune, every hardship and ease from Heaven, principle fixed in an earlier term, nothing not arriving in darkness—

sentences.zh: 玉門犁丘，睿識弗免。

translations.literal: Yumen and Líqiū—sagely insight could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Yumen Pass and Líqiū—sagely insight could not escape.

sentences.zh: 豈非聖愚齊致，仁虐同功。

translations.literal: Is it not that sage and fool reach the same end, benevolence and cruelty share the same effect?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not that sage and fool reach the same end, benevolence and cruelty share the same effect?

sentences.zh: 昏明之用，將何施而可？

translations.literal: Of what use is the function of darkness and brightness—what may still be applied?
translations.idiomatic: Of what use is the function of darkness and brightness—what may still be applied?

sentences.zh: 對曰：夫聖人懷虛以涵育，凝明以洞照。

translations.literal: The reply came: The sage embraces emptiness to nourish and condenses clarity to illuminate.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: The sage embraces emptiness to nourish and condenses clarity to illuminate.

sentences.zh: 惟虛也，故無往而不通；

translations.literal: Only through emptiness is there nowhere he does not penetrate;
translations.idiomatic: Only through emptiness is there nowhere he does not penetrate;

sentences.zh: 惟明也，故無來而不燭。

translations.literal: only through clarity is there nothing coming that he does not illumine.
translations.idiomatic: only through clarity is there nothing coming that he does not illumine.

sentences.zh: 涸海流金，弗染溫涼之岨；

translations.literal: When seas dry and metal flows, he is not stained by the slopes of warmth and coolness;
translations.idiomatic: When seas dry and metal flows, he is not stained by the slopes of warmth and coolness;

sentences.zh: 嚴兵猛兕，無累爪刃之災。

translations.literal: strict troops and fierce rhinoceroses bring no calamity of claw and blade upon him.
translations.idiomatic: strict troops and fierce rhinoceroses bring no calamity of claw and blade upon him.

sentences.zh: 忘生而生愈全，遺神而神彌暢。

translations.literal: Forgetting life, life is all the more whole; abandoning spirit, spirit is all the more free.
translations.idiomatic: Forgetting life, life is all the more whole; abandoning spirit, spirit is all the more free.

sentences.zh: 若玉門犁丘，蓋同跡於人，故同人有患，然而均心於天，亦均天無害。

translations.literal: As for Yumen and Líqiū, they share the same tracks as other men; thus other men have afflictions—yet when the heart is equalized with Heaven, Heaven too is equalized and harmless.
translations.idiomatic: As for Yumen Pass and Líqiū, they share the same tracks as other men; thus other men have afflictions—yet when the heart is equalized with Heaven, Heaven too is equalized and harmless.

sentences.zh: 大賢則體備形器，慮盡藏假，靜默以居否，深拱以違礥，皆數在清全，故鐘茲妙識。

translations.literal: The great worthy then embodies form and vessel, exhausts thought in hidden temporality, dwells in silence to abide in obstruction, deep-bows to avoid thunder—all numbers lie in pure completeness, hence he receives this subtle understanding.
translations.idiomatic: The great worthy embodies form and vessel, exhausts thought in hidden temporality, dwells in silence to abide in obstruction, deep-bows to avoid thunder—all numbers lie in pure completeness, hence he receives this subtle understanding.

sentences.zh: 是以稟仲尼之道，不在奔車之上；

translations.literal: Therefore receiving Confucius's Way, one is not upon a racing carriage;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore receiving Confucius's Way, one is not upon a racing carriage;

sentences.zh: 資伯夷之運，不處覆舟之下。

translations.literal: relying on Boyi's fortune, one is not beneath an overturned boat.
translations.idiomatic: relying on Boyi's fortune, one is not beneath an overturned boat.

sentences.zh: 若乃越難趨險，逡巡弗獲，履危踐機，黽勉從事，愚之所司，聖亦何為。

translations.literal: As for crossing hardship and rushing toward danger, hesitating without attainment, treading peril and stepping on triggers, striving diligently in affairs—what fools manage, what would the sage do?
translations.idiomatic: As for crossing hardship and rushing toward danger, hesitating without attainment, treading peril and stepping on triggers, striving diligently in affairs—what fools manage, what would the sage do?

sentences.zh: 及中下之流，馳心妄動，是非舛幹，倚伏移貿，故北宮意逆而功順，東門心晦而跡明；

translations.literal: As for the middle and lower ranks, the heart races in reckless motion, right and wrong are crossed, leaning and lying shift their trade—thus Beigong's intent was contrary yet his achievement followed, Dongmen's heart was obscure yet his traces were bright;
translations.idiomatic: As for the middle and lower ranks, the heart races in reckless motion, right and wrong are crossed, leaning and lying shift their trade—thus Beigong's intent was contrary yet his achievement followed, Dongmen's heart was obscure yet his traces were bright;

sentences.zh: 宣應遺筮而逢吉，張松協數而遘禍。

translations.literal: Xuan Ying abandoned divination yet met with good fortune; Zhang Song conformed to numbers yet encountered calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Ying abandoned divination yet met with good fortune; Zhang Song conformed to numbers yet encountered calamity.

sentences.zh: 且智防有紀，患累無方。

translations.literal: Moreover, wisdom's defenses have their rule, but the accumulation of calamity has no fixed form.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, wisdom's defenses have their rule, but the accumulation of calamity has no fixed form.

sentences.zh: 爾乃猘狗逐而華子奔，腐鼠遺而虞氏滅；

translations.literal: Then the mad dog pursued and Master Hua fled; a rotten rat was left behind and the house of Yu perished;
translations.idiomatic: Then the mad dog pursued and Master Hua fled; a rotten rat was left behind and the house of Yu perished;

sentences.zh: 匣猿逸而林木殘，櫝珠亡而池水竭。

translations.literal: the caged ape escaped and the forest trees were ruined; the casket pearl was lost and the pool water dried up.
translations.idiomatic: the caged ape escaped and the forest trees were ruined; the casket pearl was lost and the pool water dried up.

sentences.zh: 凡厥條流，曲難詳備，搖形役思，其效安征。

translations.literal: All such categories and streams are hard to set forth in full detail; to shake the form and enslave thought—what effect can be verified?
translations.idiomatic: All such categories and streams are hard to set forth in full detail; to shake the form and enslave thought—what effect can be verified?

sentences.zh: 豈若澡雪靈府，洗練神宅，據道為心，依德為慮，使跡窮則義斯暢，身泰則理兼通，豈不美哉！

translations.literal: How much better to bathe and purify the spirit's dwelling, wash and refine the soul's abode, take the Way as heart and rely on virtue for thought—so that when traces reach their end, righteousness unfolds, and when the body is at peace, principle is fully penetrated—is this not beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: How much better to bathe and purify the spirit's dwelling, wash and refine the soul's abode, take the Way as heart and rely on virtue for thought—so that when traces reach their end, righteousness unfolds, and when the body is at peace, principle is fully penetrated—is this not beautiful!

sentences.zh: 何必遺此而取彼。

translations.literal: Why must one abandon this and take that?
translations.idiomatic: Why must one abandon this and take that?

sentences.zh: 問曰：夫建極開化，樹聲貽則，典防之興，由來尚矣。

translations.literal: A question says: Establishing the pole, opening transformation, planting reputation and bequeathing norms—the rise of canonical standards has been honored from of old.
translations.idiomatic: The questioner asked: Establishing the pole, opening transformation, planting reputation and bequeathing norms—the rise of canonical standards has been honored from of old.

sentences.zh: 必乃幽符懸兆，冥數指期，善惡前征，是非素定，名教之道，不亦幾乎息哉！

translations.literal: If hidden signs hang as omens, dark numbers point to their term, good and evil are foreshadowed beforehand, right and wrong are fixed in advance—would not the Way of name and teaching nearly cease!
translations.idiomatic: If hidden signs hang as omens, dark numbers point to their term, good and evil are foreshadowed beforehand, right and wrong are fixed in advance—would not the Way of name and teaching nearly cease!

sentences.zh: 對曰：天生蒸民，樹之物則，教義所稟，豈非冥數。

translations.literal: The reply came: Heaven gave birth to the multitude and planted for them things and norms; what teaching and righteousness bestow—is this not dark number?
translations.idiomatic: He replied: Heaven gave birth to the multitude and planted for them things and norms; what teaching and righteousness bestow—is this not dark number?

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 形氣之具，必有待而存；

translations.literal: The equipment of form and qi must have something to rely on in order to exist;
translations.idiomatic: The equipment of form and qi must have something to rely on in order to exist;

sentences.zh: 顓蒙之倫，豈無因而立。

translations.literal: the class of the obstinately ignorant—how could they stand without cause?
translations.idiomatic: the class of the obstinately ignorant—how could they stand without cause?

sentences.zh: 必假纖紈以安生，藉梁豢以延祀，資信禮以繕性，秉廉義以劾情。

translations.literal: They must borrow fine silk to settle life, rely on rich grain and meat to extend sacrifice, draw on faith and ritual to repair nature, hold integrity and righteousness to restrain feeling.
translations.idiomatic: They must borrow fine silk to settle life, rely on rich grain and meat to extend sacrifice, draw on faith and ritual to repair nature, hold integrity and righteousness to restrain feeling.

sentences.zh: 聖人聰明深懿，履道測化，通體天地，同情日月，仰觀俯察，撫運裁風。

translations.literal: The sage is intelligent and deeply refined, treads the Way and fathoms transformation, penetrates the body of Heaven and Earth, shares feeling with sun and moon, looks up and down, strokes fortune and trims the wind.
translations.idiomatic: The sage is intelligent and deeply refined, treads the Way and fathoms transformation, penetrates the body of Heaven and Earth, shares feeling with sun and moon, looks up and down, strokes fortune and trims the wind.

sentences.zh: 於是乎昭日星之紀，正霜雨之度，張雲霞之明，衍風露之渥，浮舟翼滯，騰駕振幽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he displays the records of sun and stars, corrects the measures of frost and rain, spreads the brightness of clouds and mist, extends the richness of wind and dew, floats boats to wing the stagnant, rises in carriage to shake the hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he displays the records of sun and stars, corrects the measures of frost and rain, spreads the brightness of clouds and mist, extends the richness of wind and dew, floats boats to wing the stagnant, rises in carriage to shake the hidden.

sentences.zh: 又乃甄理三才，辨綜五德，弘鋪七體之端，宣昭八經之緒。

translations.literal: Moreover he discriminates and orders the three powers, distinguishes and synthesizes the five virtues, broadly spreads the beginnings of the seven categories, proclaims the threads of the eight classics.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he discriminates and orders the three powers, distinguishes and synthesizes the five virtues, broadly spreads the beginnings of the seven categories, proclaims the threads of the eight classics.

sentences.zh: 是以時雍在運，群方自通，抱德煬和，全真保性。

translations.literal: Thus harmony in season lies in fortune, the myriad directions of themselves penetrate, embracing virtue and spreading harmony, preserving the whole and guarding nature.
translations.idiomatic: Thus harmony in season lies in fortune, the myriad directions of themselves penetrate, embracing virtue and spreading harmony, preserving the whole and guarding nature.

sentences.zh: 故信食相資，代為脣齒；

translations.literal: Therefore faith and sustenance assist each other, generation after generation as lips and teeth;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore faith and sustenance assist each other, generation after generation as lips and teeth;

sentences.zh: 富教相假，遞成輔車。

translations.literal: wealth and teaching borrow from each other, in turn becoming chariot and escort.
translations.idiomatic: wealth and teaching borrow from each other, in turn becoming chariot and escort.

sentences.zh: 今弛棄纖紈，損絕梁豢，必雲徼生委命，豈不已曉其迷。

translations.literal: Now to relax and abandon fine silk, to damage and cut off rich grain and meat, and then say one entrusts life to fate—is this not already to show one's delusion?
translations.idiomatic: Now to relax and abandon fine silk, to damage and cut off rich grain and meat, and then say one entrusts life to fate—is this not already to show one's delusion?

sentences.zh: 至乎湮斥廉義，屏黜信禮，責以祈存推數，遂乃未辨其惑；

translations.literal: As for burying and rejecting integrity and righteousness, screening out faith and ritual, yet charging one to pray for preservation and push numbers—then one has still not distinguished one's delusion;
translations.idiomatic: As for burying and rejecting integrity and righteousness, screening out faith and ritual, yet charging one to pray for preservation and push numbers—then one has still not distinguished one's delusion;

sentences.zh: 連類若斯，乖妄滋甚。

translations.literal: linking categories like these, perversity and error grow all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Linking categories like these, perversity and error grow all the more.

sentences.zh: 然則教義之道，生運所資，寵辱榮枯，常由此作。

translations.literal: Thus the Way of teaching and righteousness is what life and fortune rely on; favor and disgrace, glory and withering, constantly arise from this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Way of teaching and righteousness is what life and fortune rely on; favor and disgrace, glory and withering, constantly arise from this.

sentences.zh: 斯固命中之一物，非所以為難也。

translations.literal: This is surely one thing within allotted fate, not what makes the matter difficult.
translations.idiomatic: This is surely one thing within allotted fate, not what makes the matter difficult.

sentences.zh: 問曰：循複前旨，既以理命縣兆，生數冥期。

translations.literal: A question says: Following and repeating your earlier meaning, you have already hung omens on principle and fate, and set life's numbers in a dark term.
translations.idiomatic: The questioner asked: Following and repeating your earlier meaning, you have already hung omens on principle and fate, and set life's numbers in a dark term.

sentences.zh: 研覆後文，又雲依杖名教，帥循訓範。

translations.literal: Studying and reviewing your later text, you also say one should lean on name and teaching and lead by following norms.
translations.idiomatic: Studying and reviewing your later text, you also say one should lean on name and teaching and lead by following norms.

sentences.zh: 若藉數任天，則放情蕩思；

translations.literal: If one relies on numbers and entrusts oneself to Heaven, then feeling is released and thought roams free;
translations.idiomatic: If one relies on numbers and entrusts oneself to Heaven, then feeling is released and thought roams free;

sentences.zh: 拘訓馴範，則防慮檢喪。

translations.literal: if one is bound by instruction and tamed by norms, then defenses of thought are checked and lost.
translations.idiomatic: if one is bound by instruction and tamed by norms, then defenses of thought are checked and lost.

sentences.zh: 函矢殊用，矛戈異適，雙美之談，豈能兩遂。

translations.literal: The chest-arrow has a different use, spear and dagger-axe a different application—the talk of double beauty, how can both be fulfilled?
translations.idiomatic: The chest-arrow has a different use, spear and dagger-axe a different application—the talk of double beauty, how can both be fulfilled?

sentences.zh: 對曰：夫性運乖舛，心貌詭殊，請布末懷，略言其要。

translations.literal: The reply came: Nature and fortune diverge and clash, mind and appearance are strange and different—allow me to set forth my final thoughts and speak briefly of the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: Nature and fortune diverge and clash, mind and appearance are strange and different—allow me to set forth my final thoughts and speak briefly of the essentials.

sentences.zh: 若乃吉命所鐘，縱情蹈道，訓性而順，因心則靈。

translations.literal: As for those whom fortunate fate has marked, they release feeling and tread the Way, train nature and follow it, rely on the heart and thereby become numinous.
translations.idiomatic: As for those whom fortunate fate has marked, they release feeling and tread the Way, train nature and follow it, rely on the heart and thereby become numinous.

sentences.zh: 凶數所挻，率由踐逆，聞言不信，長惡無悛。

translations.literal: Those whom ill-fated numbers extend follow the path of treading rebellion, hear words and do not believe, nurture evil without repentance.
translations.idiomatic: Those whom ill-fated numbers extend follow the path of treading rebellion, hear words and do not believe, nurture evil without repentance.

sentences.zh: 此愚智不移，聲訓所遺者也。

translations.literal: This is what the foolish and the wise do not alter—what voice and instruction leave behind.
translations.idiomatic: This is what the foolish and the wise do not alter—what voice and instruction leave behind.

sentences.zh: 其有見善如不及，從諫如順流，是則命待教全，運須化立。

translations.literal: Those who see good as if they cannot reach it, who follow remonstrance as if downstream—then fate awaits teaching to be made whole, fortune needs transformation to be established.
translations.idiomatic: Those who see good as if they cannot reach it, who follow remonstrance as if downstream—then fate awaits teaching to be made whole, fortune needs transformation to be established.

sentences.zh: 譬以良醫之室，病者所存，至如澄神清魂，平心實氣，無妄之痾，勿藥有喜，所謂縱情蹈道，無假隱括。

translations.literal: It is like a good physician's chamber where the sick are kept; as for clarifying spirit and purifying soul, leveling heart and solidifying qi—illness without recklessness needs no medicine yet brings joy; this is what is called releasing feeling and treading the Way, with no need for hidden braces.
translations.idiomatic: It is like a good physician's chamber where the sick are kept; as for clarifying spirit and purifying soul, leveling heart and solidifying qi—illness without recklessness needs no medicine yet brings joy; this is what is called releasing feeling and treading the Way, with no need for hidden braces.

sentences.zh: 若膏肓之疾，長桑不治，體府之病，陽慶弗理，此則率由踐逆，自絕調禦。

translations.literal: If it is an illness in the vital region, Chang Sang will not treat it; if it is a disease of the body's dwelling, Yang Qing will not attend—this then follows the path of treading rebellion and cuts off regulation and healing of itself.
translations.idiomatic: If it is an illness in the vital region, Chang Sang will not treat it; if it is a disease of the body's dwelling, Yang Qing will not attend—this then follows the path of treading rebellion and cuts off regulation and healing of itself.

sentences.zh: 至乃趙儲之命宜永，須扁鵲而後全，齊後之數必延，待文摯而後濟。

translations.literal: As for the fate of Prince Chu of Zhao, it should have been long—only after Bian Que was it made whole; the numbers of the Queen of Qi were bound to extend—only after Wen Zhi was it brought to completion.
translations.idiomatic: As for the fate of Prince Chu of Zhao, it should have been long—only after Bian Que was it made whole; the numbers of the Queen of Qi were bound to extend—only after Wen Zhi was it brought to completion.

sentences.zh: 亦猶運鐘循獎，彝範所興，善惡無主，唯運所集而異。

translations.literal: It is also like fortune's bell and following reward, what constant norms give rise to—good and evil have no master; only what fortune gathers makes them differ.
translations.idiomatic: It is also like fortune's bell and following reward, what constant norms give rise to—good and evil have no master; only what fortune gathers makes them differ.

sentences.zh: 膏梁方丈，沈疾弗顧；

translations.literal: rich grain and meat within a square foot, sinking illness is not regarded;
translations.idiomatic: A table laden with rich grain and meat, yet sinking illness is not regarded;

sentences.zh: 瑤碧盈尺，阽危弗存。

translations.literal: jade and greenstone filling a foot, imminent peril is not preserved.
translations.idiomatic: jade and greenstone filling a foot, imminent peril is not preserved.

sentences.zh: 夫靜躁之容，造次必於是；

translations.literal: As for the bearing of stillness and agitation, in every hasty moment one must be thus;
translations.idiomatic: As for the bearing of stillness and agitation, in every hasty moment one must be thus;

sentences.zh: 曲直之性，顛沛不可移。

translations.literal: the nature of crooked and straight, in overturning hardship cannot be shifted.
translations.idiomatic: the nature of crooked and straight, in overturning hardship cannot be shifted.

sentences.zh: 是以夷、惠均聖而異方；

translations.literal: Thus Boyi and Hui were both sages yet of different ways;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Boyi and Hui were both sages, yet they followed different paths;

sentences.zh: 遵、竦齊通而殊事。

translations.literal: Zun and Song were equally penetrating yet of distinct affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zun and Song were equally penetrating in understanding, yet pursued different courses.

sentences.zh: 雖複鉗桎羿、帟，思服巢、許之情；

translations.literal: Though one might fetter Yi and Kuai and think to adopt the mind of Chao and Xu;
translations.idiomatic: Though one might fetter Yi and Kuai and imagine adopting the spirit of Chao Fu and Xu You;

sentences.zh: 捶勒曾、史，言膺蹻、蹠之慮。

translations.literal: beat and restrain Zeng and Shi yet speak of embracing the concerns of Bo Yi and Robber Zhi—
translations.idiomatic: beat and restrain Zeng Shen and Shi Qiu yet claim to embrace the concerns of Bo Yi and Robber Zhi—

sentences.zh: 不然之事，斷可知也。

translations.literal: such things that are not so can be decisively known.
translations.idiomatic: such impossibilities can be known for certain.

sentences.zh: 必幽符鑽仰，冥數修習，雖存陵惰，其可得乎！

translations.literal: If one must have dark signs to drill into and dark numbers to cultivate, though one preserves arrogance and sloth, how could it be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: If one must have hidden omens to pore over and hidden numbers to cultivate, how could arrogance and sloth ever yield the desired result!

sentences.zh: 故運屬波流，勢無防慮，命徼山立，理無放情。

translations.literal: Therefore fortune belongs to the flowing waves—its momentum admits no guarding thought; fate is drawn like mountains standing—principle admits no unrestrained feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore fortune belongs to the flowing waves, and its momentum admits no defensive calculation. Fate stands like mountains, and principle admits no unrestrained indulgence.

sentences.zh: 用殊函矢，雙美奚躓；

translations.literal: Uses differ like arrow and sheath—how could both beauties stumble?
translations.idiomatic: Their uses differ like arrow and sheath—why should both beauties fail?

sentences.zh: 談異矛戈，兩濟何傷。

translations.literal: Discourse differs like spear and dagger—what harm if both succeed?
translations.idiomatic: Their approaches differ like spear and dagger—what harm if both succeed?

sentences.zh: 問曰：夫君臣恩深，師資義固，所以沾榮塗施，提飾荷聲。

translations.literal: A question says: Between ruler and minister the grace is deep; between teacher and pupil the righteousness is firm—therefore they are moistened with glory and spread with adornment, lifted with ornament and bearing reputation.
translations.idiomatic: A questioner asks: Between ruler and minister the bond of grace runs deep; between teacher and pupil the tie of righteousness is firm. That is why they are adorned with glory, elevated with honor, and bear reputation upon their shoulders.

sentences.zh: 故刳心流腸，捐生以亢節；

translations.literal: Therefore they cut open heart and pour forth entrails, casting away life to uphold integrity;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore they lay bare heart and entrails and cast away life to uphold their integrity;

sentences.zh: 火妻灰子，霾名以償義。

translations.literal: burning wife and reducing sons to ash, burying name to repay righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: burning their wives and reducing their sons to ash, burying their names to repay righteousness.

sentences.zh: 若幽期天兆，則明揚可遺；

translations.literal: If dark terms and heavenly omens govern, then bright promotion may be abandoned;
translations.idiomatic: If dark terms and heavenly omens govern all, then bright promotion may be set aside;

sentences.zh: 冥數自賓，則感效宜絕。

translations.literal: if dark numbers make themselves guests, then moved response and effect should cease.
translations.idiomatic: if dark numbers determine everything, then heartfelt response and loyal service should cease.

sentences.zh: 豈其然乎？

translations.literal: Could it really be so?
translations.idiomatic: Could it really be so?

sentences.zh: 對曰：論之所明，原本以為理，難之所疑，即末以為用。

translations.literal: The reply says: What the discourse clarifies takes the root and origin as principle; what the difficulty doubts takes the branch and tip as application.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: What the discourse clarifies takes root and origin as its principle; what the difficulty questions takes branch and tip as its application.

sentences.zh: 蓋陰閉之巧不傳，萌漸之調長絕。

translations.literal: The craft of hidden closure is not transmitted; the long tuning of gradual sprouting is cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The craft of hidden closure is not transmitted, and the long tuning of gradual growth is cut off.

sentences.zh: 故知妄言賞理，古人所難。

translations.literal: Therefore one knows that reckless words praising principle were difficult even for the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one knows that reckless words in praise of principle were difficult even for the ancients.

sentences.zh: 吾所謂命，固以綿絡古今，彌貫終始，爰及君臣父子，師友夫妻，皆天數冥合，神運玄至。

translations.literal: What I call fate is firmly continuous through past and present, filling and penetrating beginning and end, extending to ruler and minister, father and son, teacher and friend, husband and wife—all are darkly joined by Heaven's numbers, mysteriously arrived through spirit's movement.
translations.idiomatic: What I call fate is continuous through past and present and fills beginning and end. It extends to ruler and minister, father and son, teacher and friend, husband and wife—all are darkly joined by Heaven's numbers and mysteriously brought by the movement of spirit.

sentences.zh: 逮乎睽愛離會，既命之所甄，昏爽順戾，亦運之所漸。

translations.literal: When it reaches estranged love and parting meetings, these are what fate selects; when dull and bright, obedient and rebellious, these too are what fortune gradually brings.
translations.idiomatic: When it reaches estranged love and parting meetings, these are what fate selects. When dullness and brightness, obedience and rebellion appear, these too are what fortune gradually brings.

sentences.zh: 爾乃松柳異質，薺荼殊性，故疾風知勁草，嚴霜識貞木，何異忠孝之質，資行夙昭。

translations.literal: Then pine and willow differ in substance, shepherd's purse and turnip differ in nature; therefore fierce wind knows strong grass, harsh frost recognizes steadfast trees—how does this differ from the substance of loyalty and filial piety, whose conduct has long been manifest?
translations.idiomatic: Pine and willow differ in substance; shepherd's purse and turnip differ in nature. Fierce wind reveals strong grass; harsh frost reveals steadfast trees. How does this differ from the substance of loyalty and filial piety, whose conduct has long been manifest?

sentences.zh: 至於刻志酬生，題誠複施，殉節投命，馴義忘己。

translations.literal: As for carving the will to repay life, inscribing sincerity to repay giving, dying for integrity and casting away life, taming righteousness and forgetting self—
translations.idiomatic: As for carving one's will to repay life, inscribing sincerity to repay kindness, dying for integrity and casting away life, mastering righteousness and forgetting self—

sentences.zh: 亦由石雖可毀，堅不可銷，丹雖可磨，赤不可滅。

translations.literal: it is also because stone though it can be destroyed, its hardness cannot be dissolved; cinnabar though it can be ground, its red cannot be extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: it is also because stone, though it can be destroyed, cannot lose its hardness; cinnabar, though it can be ground, cannot lose its red.

sentences.zh: 因斯而言，君臣師資，既幽期自賓，心力感效，亦冥數天兆。

translations.literal: Speaking from this, ruler and minister, teacher and pupil—since dark terms make themselves guests, the mind's strength and moved response are also dark numbers and heavenly omens.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that between ruler and minister, teacher and pupil—since dark terms govern, heartfelt effort and loyal response are likewise dark numbers and heavenly omens.

sentences.zh: 夫獨何怪哉！

translations.literal: What alone is strange!
translations.idiomatic: What is strange about that!

sentences.zh: 願字子恭，父淵之，散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Yuan, style name Zigong, father Yuanzhi, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, whose style was Zigong, was the son of Yuanzhi, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 願好學，有文辭於世。

translations.literal: Yuan loved learning and had literary compositions in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan loved learning and was known in his time for his literary compositions.

sentences.zh: 大明中，舉秀才，對策稱旨，擢為著作佐郎，太子舍人。

translations.literal: During Daming he was recommended as Cultivated Talent; his policy response pleased the emperor and he was promoted to Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library and Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daming era he was recommended as Cultivated Talent. His policy response pleased the emperor, and he was promoted to Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library and Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：孝建啟基，西楚放命，難連淮、濟，勢盛江服。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Xiaojian opened the foundation; Western Chu cast off obedience; difficulties linked Huai and Ji; momentum flourished in the Jiang regions.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: The Xiaojian era opened a new foundation. Western Chu cast off obedience, troubles linked the Huai and Ji regions, and rebel strength flourished along the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 硃修之著節漢南，劉秀之推鋒萬里，並誠載艱一，忠惟帝念。

translations.literal: Zhu Xiuzhi displayed integrity south of the Han; Liu Xiuzhi drove his spear ten thousand li—both bore sincerity through one hardship, loyalty only for the emperor's thought.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xiuzhi displayed integrity south of the Han; Liu Xiuzhi drove his forces ten thousand li. Both bore sincerity through a single hardship, loyal only to the emperor's cause.

sentences.zh: 而逾峴之鋒，戰有獨克，出硤之師，舟無只反。

translations.literal: Yet the spear beyond Xian—in battle there was solitary victory; the army out of the gorges—not a single boat returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yet beyond Xian the spear achieved victory in battle, while the army that marched out through the gorges saw not a single boat return.

sentences.zh: 雖霜霰並時，而計功則異也。

translations.literal: Though frost and sleet came together in season, in reckoning achievement they differed.
translations.idiomatic: Though frost and sleet fell in the same season, their achievements, when reckoned, were not the same.

sentences.zh: 及定終之命，等數相懸，蓋由義結蕃朝，故恩有厚薄。

translations.literal: When it came to fixing their final allotments, the equal numbers hung far apart—probably because their righteousness bound them to the court in different degrees, so grace had thick and thin.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to their final rewards, the scales hung far apart—probably because their ties to the court differed in degree, and so grace was meted out unequally.

sentences.zh: 雖故舊不遺，聞之前訓，隆名爽實，亦無取焉！

translations.literal: Though old ties were not abandoned, as heard in former instruction—exalted name with substance lost is still nothing to take!
translations.idiomatic: Though old ties were not forgotten, as former instruction teaches—a lofty name with substance lost is still nothing to admire!
